EO 13848 (foreign-election-interference emergency) sets the post-election channel: sec. 1(a) DNI assessment "Not later than 45 days after the conclusion of" the election, to the President and the Secretaries of State, Treasury, Defense, the AG and DHS; sec. 1(b) AG and DHS report "Within 45 days of receiving" that assessment, to the President and Secretaries of State, Treasury and Defense, on whether foreign interference "materially affected the security or integrity" of election infrastructure, tabulation or transmission of results; sec. 1(c) all agencies send relevant information to the DNI and reports are amended on new information; sec. 2 Treasury blocking sanctions; sec. 3 review and sanctions after the reports. "Election infrastructure" includes "voter registration databases" (sec. 8(d)); "foreign interference" includes acts with the purpose or effect of "undermining public confidence in election processes" (sec. 8(f)). For Nov 3, 2026: 1(a) due by Dec 18, 2026; 1(b) due within 45 days after 1(a) is received, about Feb 1, 2027 if 1(a) comes Dec 18; both can come earlier.

Trump says acting DNI Bill Pulte can declassify "whatever" he wants, including 2020 election records; Pulte urged naming analysts accused of hiding election-interference reporting (Politico); declassified docs show analysts concluded China did not pursue a large-scale influence effort in 2020; House Intel Democrats complain ODNI is not briefing 2026 threats, and the Foreign Malign Influence Center is being wound down (WaPo Jul 2).

Bill Pulte serves as acting DNI from about Jul 1, 2026 until Jay Clayton is sworn in on Aug 3, 2026; in that window Trump says Pulte can declassify "whatever" he wants and the Jul 16 declassified China/voter-data trove is released with Trump's speech.

Declassification marks "DECLASSIFIED BY PRESIDENT TRUMP on 3 July 2026" on the NICA (Aug 2020), NICM 2020-09381, NSA "massaged PDB" emails, Sept 2020 coordination emails, Dec 2021 NIO email; "APPROVED FOR PUBLIC RELEASE BY PRESIDENT TRUMP" on NICM 2020-003.

In a primetime address Trump says he is declassifying documents on China's alleged acquisition of U.S. voter records, calling it "the largest compromise of election data in history" (the Jul 30 White House fact sheet later says up to 220 million records; coverage of the address cites "about 200 million" in some intelligence reporting); he says a DHS review found ~278,000 noncitizens registered and that the "deep state" hid it. BBC reports Trump said 18 states' voter data was taken by China (BBC's exact words and how they relate to the Jul 30 Task Force fact sheet: see), and he says that "My administration is in the process of notifying the states whose election data was compromised by the People's Republic of China and many others," and that he will help states "fix and patch known technical vulnerabilities before the midterm elections"; "I've also ordered DHS to notify every state about noncitizens on their voter rolls and direct them to remove all ineligible voters from the lists immediately." Earlier that evening a White House official previewed "five main revelations," said 220 million files were "compromised" by China between 2020 and 2023, and said the material did not allege that votes were changed or machines hacked; the release ran to "hundreds of pages," many heavily redacted (BBC). David Becker (CEIR) on the 278,000 figure: based on commercial data, "a ton of false positives" (CBS fact check 10:45 PM). Mullin: "We know that they can change voter registration and your vote" (limiting record released by the same White House, D: the 2020 Election Day log records one real unauthorized voter-address change in a Florida county through a known state website flaw that FBI/CISA were already working, no foreign attribution, and "no significant nefarious Chinese election-related activities," Election Day Log pp.14, 25-30, 69); the declassified release includes a CISA review of vulnerabilities in election IT networks; the documents show no altered votes, and officials in 12 of 15 named states say they were never notified (R). Counterpoint (D): no released document read gives 220 million or a 2020-2023 range; the largest voter figure is 204,822,241 records of "Unspecified U.S. voter data" dated 2016 on a list a PRC actor possessed "as of [redacted] 2019" (200M Voter Records p.3, B13).

In the speech Trump claims Michigan law enforcement found a voter-registration fraud scheme by a Democratic-affiliated group but the FBI kept it from acting before the statute of limitations ran; calls mail ballots "inherently corrupt"; says ABC, NBC and CNN should lose broadcast licences for not airing the speech. Trump calls Muskegon "pay, play and cheat," says FBI agents "believed that crimes were committed" and that "The Biden Department of Justice slow-walked the investigation and killed it"; the accompanying release (folder "3. Michigan Voter-Registration Investigation") says "Director Patel is being directed to ensure that the matter is fully investigated" a White House order to reopen a case whose last document is the current FBI's own Sept 25, 2025 no-crime closing.

At the Jul 17, 2026 White House-complex briefing, and in letters to CA, NJ, NV and PA (California's is dated and was received Jul 16, ECF 149 p.3 and Weber Oct 15 letter p.1; DHS's press release on the letters is Jul 17, ECF 149 p.6 n.3), Mullin alleges "over 250,000 potential non-citizens illegally registered" ("as many as" 190,832 in CA; DHS claims ~35,000 in NJ, which NJ attributes to ~6,600 software-error registrations, and ~14,000 of varying confidence in PA, R; Nevada's figure was later called "the ceiling" and fell to 185); AP notes the claim covered states that refused to share rolls and gave no method. He says "At President Trump's direction, our cybersecurity team in CISA will release an updated election infrastructure plan" within 30 days, that CISA will offer cyber-threat resources to states that join SAVE ("if they participate in the SAVE program, we'll provide the resources and training"; "We are going to make our security enhancements mandatory"), ties election grants to cooperation, calls states refusing SAVE a "priority" for examining who voted, and says officials who refuse could face fines, penalties or prison. To voters: "If you are an illegal or you are voting illegally, we will hunt you down, we will find you and we will prosecute you" (phrase reused by Reitz Oct 19). NPR (Aug) reports DHS would release analyses during early voting and while votes are counted ("We will pursue maximum pressure on this"). Weber: her office never shared the statewide list. CISA's Sept 2026 plan p.3 confirms the Secretary tasked CISA "In July of this year" (D).

SETTING THE RECORD STRAIGHT: President Trump Declassifies Intel on Foreign Election Interference and Deep State Coverup: China "compromised U.S. voter data on a massive scale"; "obtained the personal data of 220 million American voters ... during the 2020 election cycle, representing the largest known compromise"; agencies "knew about this breach in at least 18 states"; quotes "deliberately massaged" PDB and an FBI official "running a shadow government"; Maduro "successfully developed methods to digitally alter vote totals in undetectable ways"; ~278,000 noncitizens in four states "that cooperated"; President directed DNI, DOJ, FBI and CIA to investigate the withholding, "including potential criminal charges"; calls for the SAVE America Act.

Wayne Allyn Root interview on emergency action: "stranger things have happened, OK?"; Bannon urging emergency powers for voter ID and ICE at polls; Ticktin: "it might even require, at some point, martial law."

Omar chronology: Aug 6-7 undercover HSI agent at her MN town hall (mismatched plates); Sept-Oct Mullin and Homan confirm investigation; Oct 10 Trump says Vance and "our people" looking at Omar; WH deputy homeland-security adviser Anthony Salisbury and USCIS Director Edlow reported involved; acting DAG McCotter consulted.
Trump meets GOP strategists, with Chief of Staff Wiles present, on financing competitive midterm races with MAGA Inc. funds (Common Cause complaint, citing Oct 2 reporting).
Trump said he will move to "end mail-in ballots" and sign an EO "to help bring honesty to the 2026 elections"; Reuters: pledged to end mail-in ballots and voting machines.

Census Bureau posts (Aug 18, 2026; dated "AUGUST 2026") an unauthored brief, "Noncitizen Voting in the 2020 Election, A Beginning Analysis" (approval CBDRB-FY26-0285): "over 24,000" noncitizen voter records in 2020 with "over 32 million" records still to analyze. Every federal record reaches a voter only through a match to the DataClear 2020 commercial voter file, linked by PVS to PIKs built from SSA Numident; sources are USCIS green-card/LPR records, State immigrant and nonimmigrant visas, ICE records ("foreign students, removals, and national-docket proceedings"), USCIS DACA approvals, SSA legal-alien citizenship codes and IRS ITINs ("an affirmative noncitizen signal"); ~63,800 voters naturalized before 2020 are cleared and ~7,000 of the 24,000 have no country of birth. It cites the Bureau's "crime" statistics authority and reports no false-positive rate (it cites a 2014 PVS false-match paper without applying it). NPR reports non-career staff with America First Policy Institute ties did the work; Trump says the number will "explode" (R). Title 13 bars sharing the names. Method (App. 1-2): voters are cleared on SSA citizen codes and U.S. birth (82.7% of confirmed citizens), passports and naturalization oaths; anyone found in any federal noncitizen source (including ITIN holders, DACA recipients and foreign students) is presumed a noncitizen "unless citizenship evidence establishes" otherwise; the DataClear file was bought in 2024 for undercount research.
DOE 202(c) orders keep generation on; D.C. Cir. Sept 11 vacated Campbell 202(c) order;

Notice continuing for 1 year the EO 13848 national emergency on foreign interference in or undermining public confidence in U.S. elections (FR Sept 2, 2026). EO 13848 requires a post-election DNI assessment within 45 days (~Dec 18, 2026) and an AG/DHS report within 45 days of receiving it (~Feb 1, 2027).
Truth Social announces "AI Force"; government will "not in any way hinder or stifle" AI growth.

Per the Common Cause and DNC complaints: in late September Trump told OMB Director Vought to "come up with the money" for ads "from within the government"; Sept 19 OMB raised CBP's "Commemorative Events" apportionment (line 6043, OBBBA funds) by $20M from $500K; Sept 20 DHS signed a $20M "National Media Campaign" order with LMD Agency, Inc. (70B06C26F00001137); ads praising the President aired from Sept 23. FT (AdImpact): 26 of the top 30 markets had competitive races. The ads carry the line "Paid for by the U.S. Government."
tl.a: President Trump / OMB Vought / DHS CBP / LMD Agency

tl.e: Xi arrives at Joint Base Andrews the afternoon of Sept 23, greeted by Trump and the First Lady; on Sept 25, wrapping the three-day state visit, Xi says he will meet Trump twice more in 2026 (APEC in Shenzhen in November, which Trump says he will attend; G20 at Trump National Doral a month later); the trade truce is extended to January. No mention of voter data or election interference.

Order directs agencies to use "Super Intelligence"/"SI" instead of "AI" in official communications, websites, reports and policy; science adviser to define "SI" (~late Nov); same day White House "Accord on Super Intelligence" lunch (signers reportedly Musk, Zuckerberg, Huang, Amodei, Pichai, Brockman; voluntary). Oct 8 Truth Social reportedly called anyone still saying "AI" "THE ENEMY."

EO 14434, "Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence" (91 FR 63129, Oct 2): agencies "shall use ''Super Intelligence'' and ''SI'' in place of ''Artificial Intelligence'' and ''AI''" and "will not acknowledge the usage" of the old terms; SI means what 15 U.S.C. 9401(3) calls artificial intelligence; within 60 days (about Nov 28) the President's science adviser must propose legislative language for a federal definition of SI, including whether it should "modify, expand upon, or otherwise supersede" the statutory AI definition. (D)
Did not rule out declaring a national emergency around the midterms or invoking the Insurrection Act.

Oct 3 Truth Social: "Whether you vote early, absentee, by mail, or in-person, we must 'swamp' the Radical Left Dumocrats"; same-day video "Vote early, vote by mail, or vote in person"; Oct 5: "can vote by mail if they want." Contrast Mar 11 post: "NO MAIL-IN BALLOTS (EXCEPT FOR ILLNESS, DISABILITY, MILITARY, OR TRAVEL!)"
Truth Social 8:36 a.m.: rallies/races flipping, "Watch for the 'Midterm Surprise!'"; 11:00 and 12:30 closed Oval policy meetings (schedule as given in earlier notes).
At a Maryland event, Trump says "We have some big surprises coming up in a few weeks, right Russ?" (Vought, Project 2025 author).

Common Cause v. DHS (S.D.N.Y. 26-cv-8882) complaint over taxpayer-funded ads (filed about Oct 7, 2026; filing day not confirmed on the S.D.N.Y. docket) alleges an Aug 7 meeting (Wiles present, $400M of MAGA Inc. money discussed) and that Trump told Vought to find money for the ads "from within the government"; Judge Rochon's Oct 11 TRO is its own row.
Trump announces diesel-import deal with Russia after Putin call (Oct 9); "energy ceasefire" (Oct 11) after urging Zelenskyy to stop striking Russian energy.

Common Cause v. DHS (S.D.N.Y. 26-cv-8882): TRO ordering administration to stop airing and "cancel or cause to be cancelled" government-funded pro-Trump ads; barred use of DHS funds for them; complaint cites NYT Oct 2 (Haberman) for Aug 7 meeting where Trump told Vought to find money "from within the government."
Trump reposts DOJ letter: "They will all go to jail for a long period of time!!!"
Putin proposed a three-way summit (~Oct 18-19); Trump said ~Oct 20 he was open to a "denuclearization" summit; APEC Shenzhen Nov 18-19; G20 at Doral in December.
Kansas rally: "A lot of the polls are rigged, just like the journalists are rigged."
Trump: "I will be the arbitrator of all of these decisions," 1% of reported fraud, no cap; McDonald: "enlist the public as part of the fraud-fighting apparatus."

Announcing the Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program, Trump says whistleblowers get 1% of reported fraud with no limit, that criminal charges are not necessary, "You'll get your money immediately," and that he will decide "whether or not the person is deserving" ("I will be the arbitrator"); the written DOJ program caps awards at $10,000-$30,000 paid when charges are filed. The first check ($10,000) is handed to YouTuber Nick Shirley.
Fort Myers: Rep. Omar "has openly admitted to fraud, and she will not be legally allowed to be a member."
Port Huron, MI: Trump attacks Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed's "loyalty," portrays him as a national-security threat.

Truth Social: "Anybody reporting Voter Fraud in the past Elections, or the upcoming 2026 Midterm Election, will be paid $1,000,000" on arrest and conviction; Trump to be "the arbitrator"; no funding, agency, intake channel or criteria given.

Asked before leaving for Texas rallies whether he will respect the midterm results, Trump says "I will if they're honest elections," and that if Democrats win "We'll figure a way," citing his veto power.

TIME: Trump doesn't "rule anything out," including a federal emergency declaration or ICE agents at polls; allies urging martial law to seize ballots; Gen. Caine said military has "no plan" to deploy to polls; at least three suits seek to block ICE from polling sites (one cites a Colorado sheriff's "warrant checks at polling locations"); Arlington County planning for federal agents.

After an NYT report that Peltola's campaign helped recruit a second "Dan Sullivan," Trump says Peltola "should be prosecuted criminally" and should resign, and posts "She shouldn't be allowed to run"; Blanche on Fox says the recruitment "should be illegal" and points to DOJ's civil suit to block certification.

Trump posts that the Acting U.S. Attorney in Los Angeles "caught a massive number of Illegal Votes, 20,000, but potentially Hundreds of Thousands, and maybe even Millions, and the Court has just ruled against it. Why would they reject fixing Election Fraud?"

Presidential Message on Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience Month: "Our goal is clear: to secure the supply chains and systems on which our Nation depends so that no adversary and no disaster will ever hold America or our core interests hostage."

On the eve of the election, U.S. forces strike Iran's Qeshm Island (Strait of Hormuz) in what a U.S. official calls a "defensive" response to Iranian fire at a U.S. aircraft, amid an ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict and Qatar-brokered talks; Trump says "One way or the other, we will do something, but there is no rush"; AP reports Israel pressing for a larger air campaign after the Nov 3 midterms.

DOJ press release (Nov 2): "charges involving 63 individuals, including four illegal aliens, in connection with illegal voting, fraudulent voter registration, and related election crimes" in about 20 federal districts. Blanche: "Today's announcement marks the largest surge of voter-fraud arrests since President Trump returned to office"; "These foreign nationals allegedly took advantage of the trust of the American people"; DOJ "will continue investigating and prosecuting voter fraud to restore confidence in our electoral system." Also: "In the last nine weeks alone, the Department has charged 195 aliens across 25 states"; "Since the beginning of this Administration, we have charged 239 people." The case list names each person with age and nationality, and the release carries photos of individuals. By our count of the case descriptions, at least 54 of the 63 are described as lawful permanent residents (green-card holders); the conduct described is mostly in the 2024 election or earlier, some going back to 2000.

FBI arrests Oklahoma City man Robin Martin (Nov 2) on charges of "conveying a hoax and mailing threatening communications"; an FBI affidavit made public Nov 3 links more than 700 mailings this fall, many with nonhazardous white powder, to election officials, members of Congress, pollsters, news media and federal law enforcement including Director Patel. Letters warned "Stay on the right side of history! Your life may depend on it!!"; the affidavit says the writer "claimed that President Donald Trump won the 2020 election."

About 1 a.m. on Election Day Trump posts on Truth Social that "FAKE ALASKA CANDIDATE DANIAL J. SULLIVAN, JR., IS MISSING IN ACTION" and that "CORRUPT DUMOCRAT LAWYERS" are "SCARED STIFF OF BEING PROSECUTED"; asked whether he will respect results, he says he will "if they are honest elections."

Guam posts unofficial results first. Delegate to the U.S. House (non-voting): Democrat Alicia Limtiaco 15,645 (51%) to Republican incumbent James Moylan 14,983 (48.84%), a 662-vote lead in final unofficial results; governor: Republican Tony Ada leads Democrat Therese Terlaje 15,945 to 14,925. Both unofficial until the Guam Election Commission certifies; no race call by a news organization found. Trump on Truth Social: Guam "just had an early call for a Republican Victory in the top spot, Governor"; "Congratulations to Tony Ada!"; "hopefully that's an indication for things to come!"

In a 4:11 p.m. ET Truth Social video, Trump says the RNC's election integrity team was "on the ground immediately" after Westchester County "wasn't able to scan ballots"; on Pennsylvania mail ballots: "I don't believe it's humanly possible to get a 120,000" returned on time; urges viewers to report problems at protectthevote.com if "something goes wrong"; claims Republicans flipped Guam. No explicit fraud allegation and no federal action described.

DOJ sends letters to about 20 Democrats telling them they may be targets of a criminal investigation into the recruitment of a second "Dan Sullivan" in Alaska's Senate race; intended recipients reportedly include elections lawyer Marc Elias and at least one DSCC official (two anonymous sources; DOJ declined comment). Reported focus: possible donor fraud and conspiracy; no statutes cited publicly. Trump said Elias "should go to jail, in my opinion" and that Schumer and Elias should be held "criminally responsible."

In a phone interview with CBS (Robert Costa), Trump said he would use "tremendous executive powers" if Democrats obstruct him or open oversight investigations, citing the Supreme Court's June Trump v. Slaughter ruling; separately welcomed the "Mr. Veto" label (R, IBTimes UK Nov 4). Nov 4: impeachment worry "Not even a little bit" (R, ABC AU).

The AP calls the Senate for Democrats late Nov 3 (after the Iowa race) and the House early Nov 4. Trump first posts: "I wasn't on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!"; then tells the New York Times: "I am absolutely willing to accept those results" and "We'll work with the Democrats ... We'll probably work something out"; he also posts a red hat reading "VETO." Results delays expected in Westchester County, N.Y. (machine issues).

Asked about the losses, Trump told Fox News "I think a part of it was Iran" and the WSJ "Iran was a piece of it", meaning the war with Iran, not interference; he also told POLITICO "I don't want to be just sitting there for two years vetoing everything."
Trump calls for Alaska to transfer to Sen. Dan Sullivan all votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan (R).

District of Delaware creates a Program Fraud Task Force (first meeting Oct 29) with the Fraud Division, "more than a dozen federal law enforcement agencies, and multiple state law enforcement agencies"; it is "part of a nationwide initiative" and "supports President Trump's Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance." West Virginia's two U.S. Attorneys created a statewide fraud task force the same season (R, WVNS).
tl.a: U.S. Attorney Benjamin L. Wallace (D. Del.); DOJ National Fraud Enforcement Division; state law enforcement agencies

tl.e: Truth Social (shown "6d" on Nov 13): "The threats being made by the Democrat Party against innocent Republican Donors and Party Members are absolutely unprecedented, and totally illegal. Please report them to the Department of Justice, IMMEDIATELY! If you would like, send them directly to me, your President. These SLEAZEBAGS should go to jail for what they are doing. The Senate must act ... Likewise, the DOJ and House of Representatives."
President Trump nominates Michael LoSapio, chief information security officer at Palantir, to be CISA director, replacing acting director Nick Andersen if confirmed. (R)

Trump posts (Nov 9): "Does anybody really believe that this 'Election' was honest ... Some early voting 'dumps' were so large that it was impossible to win," and revives voting-machine claims; (Nov 10): votes for Daniel J. Sullivan and Gerald Heikes "should immediately be given to the Real Dan Sullivan (Senator!)" and "There should be no question concerning this Rigged Election." (R)

ProPublica (Nov 9; summarized by Political Wire, Medical Daily, Sahara Reporters): "The Trump administration awarded a small biosecurity company nearly $40 million to screen for Ebola and other infectious diseases just months after a firm linked to President Donald Trump's elder sons invested in its parent company." An $18.8M CDC contract for Ebola entry screening at U.S. airports and a $20M State Department contract for outbreak response in the Democratic Republic of Congo, "seven times the total value of government contracts the company had directly received before." American Ventures, a fund launched by Dominari Holdings (offices in Trump Tower; Trump Jr. and Eric Trump hold advisory roles and stakes over 10%), invested about $30M in XWELL in February 2026. XpresTest "has never worked on Ebola or provided biosecurity services abroad"; the CEO called the international work "a new thing for us." XWELL announced in July a $13M sale of XpresTest; Ernst said the contracts "played a role" in the price.
tl.a: XpresTest / XWELL (CEO Scott Ernst); American Ventures (Dominari Holdings; Donald Trump Jr., Eric Trump); CDC; State Department

tl.e: Scharf letter to incoming House Oversight chair Robert Garcia: "The Administration will not be extorted and will not be cowed by unlawful process"; oversight investigations may "cross the line into blatant criminality"; cites Trump v. Mazars. Garcia: "It appears Donald Trump has something to hide."
tl.a: White House counsel William O. Scharf

tl.e: Judge Thomas Matthews grants the Division of Elections summary judgment (17-page order, read): the case is "fundamentally a public records case"; preliminary rejection lists are not final "public records." He rules the Peltola campaign's request for a list of rejected absentee ballots "not reasonable" given the count; records "cannot reasonably be produced at this juncture." Peltola leads Sen. Sullivan by about 4,000 and both Sullivans combined by 223 at 84% counted; Trump posted inaccurate totals Tuesday; tabulation Nov 18, certification Nov 25.
tl.a: Alaskans for Mary v. Dahlstrom (Alaska Super. Ct. 3AN-26-10304CI, Judge Matthews)

tl.e: Reported (NYT, then NY Post): Habba Mildon, then a senior adviser to Attorney General Bondi overseeing U.S. attorneys, took a general-counsel job with Concord Partners, founded by the daughter of Venezuelan banker Julio Herrera Velutini, reportedly $10 million a year for four years; she began Jan. 1 and weeks later Trump granted Herrera a full pardon. After Trump called the arrangement "obnoxious and outrageous," Concord fired her (Nov 11).
tl.a: Alina Habba Mildon; Concord Partners (Isabela Herrera); Julio Herrera Velutini; President Trump

tl.e: Trump on Truth Social: "I have asked Vice President Vance to focus his complete and total attention on the Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States throughout the U.S."; "The Blue States, such as Minnesota, California, Illinois, and many more, are all poorly run, corrupt disasters. Billions of Dollars is being stolen each and every month"; "We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed." NPR: the assignment Trump first gave Vance when he launched a fraud task force in March.
tl.a: President Trump; Vice President JD Vance

tl.e: Truth Social, 6:28 AM: Democrats, "in order to deflect from MASSIVE BLUE STATE CORRUPTION & CRIME, ... are at it again, illegally threatening Republicans with knowingly false accusations and charges. Other than cheating, this is how they won the Midterms But we won't let our Country go to hell!"

Truth Social, 7:04 AM: "With the perceived loss by the Republicans in the Midterms I WAS NOT ON THE BALLOT- the INVASION of our Country is taking place again. Huge CARAVANS are forming ... MEXICO MUST STOP THEM, NOW, and if they do not do so, the Tariffs on Mexico will be IMMEDIATELY DOUBLED. MEXICO, THE GOVERNOR OF TEXAS, THE VERY LIBERAL NEW GOVERNOR OF TEXAS, OUR GREAT BORDER PATROL, & ICE, HAVE BEEN SO INFORMED. There will be no leniency!"

Truth Social, 7:35 AM: "Not passing THE SAVE AMERICA ACT (Voter I.D., Proof of Citizenship), sent up five times by the House, was devastating to the Republican Party in the Midterms. Not terminating the Filibuster, and getting EVERYTHING even 'dreamt' of, approved, when the Dems will definitely do so, will go down as being one of the greatest mistakes in the Political History of America." Congratulates Thune "for another year of leadership, Minority though it may be!"
tl.a: President Trump; Senate Republican Leader John Thune

tl.e: Mullin at the evening White House briefing: the failure came from patching new technology into the existing framework, which overwhelmed the older system; 'We need someone to come in and build the whole system'; 'It has to be a complete overhaul of the system, which we estimate to be about $50 billion.' Duffy: routers and switches overloaded and shut down after giving inconsistent data. Trump (to Fox's Peter Doocy, paraphrased): no sign of cyberattack or AI, 'old broken stuff.' White House presidential-actions page shows no emergency declaration dated Nov 13.
tl.a: DHS Sec. Markwayne Mullin; DOT Sec. Sean Duffy; President Trump

tl.e: Per Fox's Peter Doocy on The Ingraham Angle, Trump said by phone during the outage that it did not appear to be a cyberattack or AI: "He said instead this seems to be a situation where there's a bunch of old broken stuff in the infrastructure that the FAA relies on to keep planes in the sky." Trump had not posted about the outage on Truth Social by Saturday morning; during the ground stop he met Jon Voight on a federal film incentive (Variety).

Truth Social, Nov 14 ~7:50 pm ET: "Has anyone noticed that immediately after the Election the Stock Market lost 3 Trillion Dollars in Value? In other words, Investors throughout the World hated seeing what took place on Election Day."

Truth Social, Nov 15, 8:16 and 8:35 am ET, first comments on the Nov 13 FAA ground stop: "The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster. Everything they touched turned bad"; "we need Congress to give the money, FAST!"; "it should be done all at once, not in drips and drabs. Congress must approve." He does not use "national emergency" or mention cyber.

Politico (Katherine Tully-McManus, Jennifer Scholtes) via Yahoo and The Washington Sun (Eric Katz): Trump "has nominated Eric Ueland as comptroller general and head of the Government Accountability Office"; "now Ueland is the deputy director for management at the Office of Management and Budget." HSGAC "will hold a hearing on his nomination Thursday" (Nov 19). Sun: Paul "serves as the de facto head of the statutory, bipartisan commission required to submit candidates to lead the GAO"; "Paul gave them less than 24 hours to submit names for consideration"; "Paul never convened the commission." GAO "has issued more than a half-dozen findings of illegal impoundment of federal dollars since the start of Trump's second term. But so far, GAO has not taken legal action." The job "has sat vacant since Gene Dodaro's term expired at the end of 2025." The White House floated Ueland in October (Political Wire, Oct 8).
tl.a: President Trump; Eric Ueland (OMB deputy director for management); Sen. Rand Paul (HSGAC chair); GAO; Gene Dodaro (former Comptroller General); Russ Vought (OMB director)

tl.e: On public inspection Nov 16, to publish Nov 19 (FR 2026-23529, interim final rule, RIN 0694-AK50): "Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors": licenses for overseas data centers supplying compute to companies headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau ("advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors"), and a new license requirement for Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil "(and any additional country designated by the Secretary of Commerce)"; the five-country requirement "will not apply to semiconductors destined to companies headquartered in ... the United States," and the rule exempts "commercial recommender systems, such as those used by online retailers or social media companies." Same day (R, headlines): WaPo, "Trump's stake in Nvidia grew to as much as $62 million before scandal broke out"; Politico, "Trump says he is not firing Lutnick"; CBS, "Inside Lutnick's Commerce Department, lack of action on alleged AI chip smuggling came with a side of 'chaos,' ex-employees say"; NPR ties the rule to "Nvidia fallout."
tl.a: Commerce Department, Bureau of Industry and Security; Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick; President Trump

tl.e: Democracy Docket (Natalie Hausmann): Trump "posted a video of former Fox News host Bill O'Reilly escalating threats against Democrats"; O'Reilly: "The Democratic Party in Alaska cheated, they cheated and in a big way," "And that's going to lead to criminal prosecution." Count (Democracy Docket live blog, Nov 16 2:47 pm): "Peltola has received 140,637 votes, — 559 more than all three other candidates combined." NBC: Peltola "likely to win."
tl.a: President Trump; Bill O'Reilly; Senate candidate Mary Peltola

tl.e: CNN: new U.S. intelligence indicates Iran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials in Washington with a "dirty bomb" or chemical weapon; officials characterize it as options, not an imminent attack. White House: "monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland." Nov 17, Trump: the U.S. takes it "very seriously" and Iran would "pay a price." Iran calls the report fabricated. Same day Iran fired drones at a U.S. radar in Bahrain.
tl.a: U.S. intelligence officials (anonymous, via CNN); White House spokesperson Lauren Bis; President Trump

tl.e: DeLauro on the Ueland GAO nomination: "Even more concerning is Mr. Ueland's inability to protect the independence of the Council on Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency (CIGIE) during his term as the CIGIE's executive chair. During his tenure, the agency has seen all of its Congressionally-appropriated funding frozen by Mr. Ueland's colleagues at OMB on multiple occasions." Peters: "President Trump's nomination of Eric Ueland – and Congressional Republicans' rubber stamp of this nomination in violation of longstanding bipartisan practice" (FNN). HSGAC hearing Nov 19 with nine other nominees.
tl.a: Rep. Rosa DeLauro (House Appropriations ranking member); Sen. Gary Peters (HSGAC ranking member); Eric Ueland (OMB Deputy Director for Management; Comptroller General nominee)

tl.e: Trump heads to Asia for a three-way meeting with Xi and Putin in China; China calls it of "groundbreaking significance." (R, headlines: NPR, Reuters, CNBC, AFP)
tl.a: President Trump; Xi Jinping; Vladimir Putin

tl.e: On the run of outages (FAA, Microsoft, banks): "Things like that happen. It's fine"; "It's life." (R)

DHS/ICE/PIA-055 RAVEn base PIA signed (Chief Privacy Officer Dena Kozanas). It covers a cloud platform that bulk-ingests or API-queries DHS, other-agency and commercial data, uses AI/ML, and can share 'final analytical products' with federal, state, local, tribal and foreign law enforcement, 'relevant fusion centers, FBI Joint Terrorism Task Forces' and INTERPOL. TFOs from other DHS components can get tool access.
tl.a: ICE HSI Innovation Lab / DHS Privacy

tl.e: Told a White House lawyer who warned of riots if he became acting AG: "Well ... that's why there's an Insurrection Act" (as alleged in the Aug 1, 2023 federal indictment, where he is an unnamed co-conspirator).
tl.a: Jeffrey Clark (then DOJ Civil Division acting AAG)

tl.e: Jeffrey Clark serving as acting Administrator of OMB's Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA) by late Feb 2025 (E&E News, Feb 28, 2025); his 'acting' status later challenged by watchdogs as unlawful.

DHS/ICE-018 Analytical Records SORN published (86 FR 15246, FR Doc 2021-05651), effective on publication, with routine uses effective Apr 21, 2021. It consolidates FALCON-SA (ICE-016) and TTAR (ICE-005) into one ICE analytics system with a central data store and AI/ML. Records include SSN, passport, citizenship and nationality, biometrics, BSA data, social media, commercial data and tips. Covered individuals include people in 'passport, visa, border, immigration, naturalization benefit' data. Routine uses A-U include G (law enforcement at any level, foreign included), K (intelligence and counterterrorism to federal, state, local, foreign 'and other entities or individuals'), T (technology testing) and U (media). The RAVEn PIA cites it as RAVEn's 'potential pool of data'.
tl.a: ICE / DHS Privacy (Acting CPO James Holzer)

tl.e: Final rule adopts the ICE-018 Analytical Records exemptions as proposed (86 FR 61665, FR Doc 2021-24328), effective Nov 8, 2021. Four comments raised predictive policing and surveillance. DHS answered that the system 'does not support predictive policing' or ongoing surveillance.
ICE rescinds the ICE-005 TTAR and ICE-016 FALCON-SA SORNs and relies on ICE-018 Analytical Records for those records (87 FR 6620, effective on publication).
Plan to condition grants on sharing DMV and voter data (used in FEMA Jul 9 conditions); CISA should stay away from elections; end CYBERCOM's election role (Hegseth memo did the opposite).

Rubio roles: Secretary of State (Jan 21, 2025); acting National Security Adviser from May 1, 2025, named permanent National Security Adviser while remaining Secretary of State (reported Sept 22, 2026, same day as the Hegseth memo; signing date not stated); acting USAID administrator Feb 3-Aug 29, 2025 (handed to Vought); acting Archivist Feb 16, 2025-Feb 4, 2026.
Storch v. Hegseth (D.D.C.): the Jan 24, 2025 IG firings are held unlawful, but no one is reinstated.

Project 2025 CISA chapter: CISA "should not be significantly involved closer to an election"; DoD chapter: end USCYBERCOM participation in efforts to "fortify" elections; Hegseth Sept 22 memo moves the opposite way (military/intel up, civilian support down).
April hearing: called ballot-seizure questions a "gotcha hypothetical"; "I've never been ordered to do anything illegal."

Twenty-one Senate Democrats led by Leader Schumer and Sen. Warner write DHS Secretary Mullin, Acting AG Blanche, Defense Secretary Hegseth and the acting DNI to "preserve all existing and future records and materials on election-related activities and efforts," including records of possible election-related misconduct, meeting notes, legal opinions and messages on Signal, social media and personal email; cites the Federal Records Act (D).
tl.a: Senate Democrats (Schumer, Warner, Padilla, Schiff and 17 others)

tl.e: Dhillon 50-state letter frames "intentional act that is aimed at diluting the votes of citizens"; Hegseth Sept 22 memo uses "every lawful voter ... entirely undiluted."
tl.a: AAG Harmeet Dhillon (letter to all 50 states)

tl.e: Letters press Hegseth and Gen. Caine to commit to keeping the military out of the midterms, including seizure of "election materials of any kind"; Hegseth earlier (April hearing) called ballot-seizure question a "gotcha hypothetical."

CJCS Gen. Caine writes Sen. Slotkin that the "Joint Force has no plans to send Federal military personnel or Federalized members of the National Guard to polling places" in 2026, nor to seize ballots or voting machines, and that he has not received "any unlawful order"; Hegseth had not replied; DoD (Asst. Sec. Ditlevson) repeats it ~Oct 1.

Rep. Massie announces he will force a 34-page privileged resolution to impeach Secretary Hegseth (Sept 15-16) and House Democrats file five articles; the House takes its last votes Sept 16 and recesses until after the election, and the Speaker says the resolution will be tabled on return.

DOJ national "Enforcement Actions Related to Election Integrity" press event (Utah postal worker indicted Sept 16 for disposing of ~300 ballots, conduct Jun 3) same day Hegseth signed memo; further announcements Sept 24, 28, 30, Oct 5.
tl.a: DOJ with HSI and USPS OIG

tl.e: Hegseth signs a memo (Sept 22, 2026; released Sept 28) to the Commander USCYBERCOM, Director NSA/Chief CSS, Director DIA and Director NGA: the Defense Intelligence Enterprise is to "mobilize every authorized asset, capability, and partnership under your command to defend our election infrastructure from foreign malign influence" and "execute collection and production on foreign threats to our elections," citing "Executive direction"; CYBERCOM is to use "existing authorities, capabilities, and competencies in coordination with the Department of Homeland Security, to counter potential cyber threats from foreign actors targeting our elections"; protecting elections "is a no-fail mission and the DoW will do its part in supporting this whole of government effort," so that every lawful voter's "voice remains sovereign, secure, and entirely undiluted."
Closed briefing incl. election-security update (CYBERCOM J2/J3, DoD Cyber Policy) day after Hegseth memo.

Nextgov: ODNI overhaul shifted many Foreign Malign Influence Center duties elsewhere; ODNI 'has subsequently assigned two officials to coordinate election threat intelligence'; Hegseth memo names no adversary or operation, no staffing, funding or deadlines, and does not say whether the joint NSA-CYBERCOM Election Security Group model will be used.

Hegseth's Sept 30, 2026 memo and "State of the Force" speech at Quantico create "Project Meridian: The Future of Warfare," to "study the battlefields of the future, identify which weapons and technologies warfighters will need to harness to dominate in these environments and propose actionable solutions to start developing, testing and fielding these capabilities" (Federal News Network quoting the memo). Co-led by Musk (SpaceX), Luckey (Anduril) and Gingrich; overseen by Michael; run through MITRE as the "partner organization"; findings due Jan 28, 2027. FNN: other members include Safra Catz (Oracle), Rick Smith (Axon) and Bob Smith (Parsons); SpaceX "has received over $8 billion in defense contracts in 2026 alone."
tl.a: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth; DoD CTO / Under Secretary for Research and Engineering Emil Michael; Elon Musk; Palmer Luckey; Newt Gingrich; MITRE Corporation

tl.e: Southern-border drone ban within 1 nm north of U.S.-Mexico border, surface to 400 ft, no end date; Hegseth: "shoot down any cartel drone."

CREW, Public Citizen and POGO sue DoD, Hegseth and Michael (D.D.C., filed Nov 2) alleging Project Meridian was created and operates in violation of the Federal Advisory Committee Act and the APA: no Federal Register notice, closed meetings without written justification, no record-keeping, no conflict-of-interest provisions; DoD has not acted "to ensure that the advice and recommendations of Project Meridian will not be inappropriately influenced by the DoD or any special interest, as required by FACA." Complaint: "Nineteen of the 21 members of Project Meridian work in the private sector. Many of those members have significant financial interests in the findings and recommendations made by the committee." POGO's Scott Amey: DoD "in collaboration with MITRE, is trying to make this out to be some kind of contractor-like service." Relief sought: declare unlawful, preserve and disclose records, halt meetings until FACA compliance.
tl.a: CREW; Public Citizen; Project On Government Oversight (plaintiffs); DoD, Secretary Hegseth, Under Secretary Emil Michael (defendants); U.S. District Court for D.C.

tl.e: DHS release: a new interagency memorandum of understanding on counter-drone (C-UAS) operations, with "data sharing" among the agencies. Hegseth: "we are eliminating bureaucratic silos"; American airspace "remains sovereign, secure, and impenetrable." Patel: the FBI "seiz[ed] over 700 drones during the World Cup" with "state and local officers trained at our first of its kind National Counter-UAS Training Center." Blanche cites the FBI arrest of five men over a drone plot at a White House event. (D)
tl.a: DHS, DOT, Department of War, DOE, DOJ (White House Task Force to Restore American Airspace Sovereignty)

tl.e: On Fox News (Tucker Carlson Tonight), Vought says there is "systemic voter fraud being done in North Carolina at the State Board of Election level and the DMV," tied to non-citizens voting. On Aug 13 the NC State Board of Elections calls the claims false: the DMV citizenship pre-population problem was fixed years earlier and affected few registrants, and the suggestion it was intentional is "categorically false."

Open letter from Vought to NCSBE Executive Director Karen Brinson Bell: "There is every reason to believe your state's elections are not secure"; "the old adage 'trust, but verify' most certainly applies"; asks whether the board has run "a statewide de-duping of its voter rolls utilizing all available federal and state databases" and whether it was "denied access" to any; faults the board's SAVE audit because SAVE only returns people USCIS is "formally aware of"; asks for proof of citizenship at registration. Credits the American Accountability Foundation's records requests (a CPI partner group) for surfacing the DOJ report.
tl.a: Russ Vought (president, Citizens for Renewing America)

tl.e: Mandate for Leadership Ch.5 (Cuccinelli): move CISA to DOT; CISA "should not be significantly involved closer to an election"; FEMA grants conditioned on state "total information-sharing... access to department of motor vehicles and voter registration databases" (p.138); USCIS IC-adjacent, realign FDNS (p.152). Ch.2 (Vought) "carefully enforce the Privacy Act" (p.50). EOP chapter (Vought, printed pp.44-46): agencies run under presidential direction; aggressive use of OMB apportionment as a policy tool; political control via OMB budget review and general counsels (pages per our audit notes, not re-opened).

Vought 2023: "We want to be able to shut down the riots and not have the legal community or the defense community come in"; 2024: Democrats ensuring military won't "respond to any orders to quell any violence"; CRA drafting Insurrection Act rationale.

POLITICO reports that the Center for Renewing America (Vought's think tank) listed "invoking the Insurrection Act on Day One" among second-term priorities, alongside a "Christian nationalism" bullet and refusing to spend congressionally authorized funds (impoundment); POLITICO says the documents "do not outline specific Christian nationalist policies," and a CRA spokesperson called the reporting "false."
ProPublica: Vought's 2023-24 remarks tied military use to quelling post-election unrest and protest; his think tank drafted Insurrection Act rationale.

Recorded: building legal rationale for Insurrection Act ("shut down the riots and not have the legal community or the defense community come in"); on 2020: "that compelling case has emerged"; left uses government "until they no longer have to win elections."

Complaint: "Defendants are attempting to shutter CIGIE by taking away its Congressionally appropriated funding"; OMB did not apportion CIGIE funds Oct 1-Nov 17, 2025, then apportioned about $4.3 million through Jan 30, 2026, leaving roughly $24 million unapportioned; it quotes an OMB spokesperson: "The American people will no longer be funding this corruption." Oversight.gov (34,000+ reports) and 28 IG hotline sites went dark Oct 1 (Nextgov).
tl.a: PEER, Government Accountability Project and POGO v. OMB and Russell Vought (D. Md. 8:25-cv-04164-PX)

tl.e: On the Benny Johnson show Vance alleges immigration fraud by Rep. Omar, says he discussed it with Stephen Miller (legal remedies/case-building) and separately raises her knowledge of Minnesota benefits fraud; the fraud task force holds its first meeting the same day (Vance, Miller, Vought, Mullin, Andrew Ferguson, Colin McDonald). On May 19 Vance says DOJ is looking at the immigration allegation. Omar denies it.

Vought's FY2027 budget amendments letter to Speaker Johnson includes an amendment 'to increase the number of political staff the Department of Transportation may hire to support Federal Aviation Administration Air Traffic Control modernization efforts.'
$810M pocket rescission (immigration-related FEMA & USCIS grants); OMB removed public apportionment database.

Modern Skies Act introduced (Schmitt, with Duffy and Bedford, Sept 28): $30.1B. Reason Foundation's analysis: only about 40% goes to air traffic control; $10B for a terminal pilot at "not more than 3 transitional hub airports" run by the Office of the Secretary "rather than the FAA"; $3B AIP and a new $5B terminal program "purely discretionary"; $2B for cloud computing it calls "an unnecessary science project"; $7.2B Common Automation Platform with no Acquisition Program Baseline, all "up front"; $600M for SMART (ASI). AvWeb: the Nov 13 Duffy-Vought letter "renews that earlier proposal."
tl.a: Sen. Eric Schmitt; Transportation Sec. Sean Duffy; FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford

tl.e: Letter to Mullin demanding answers within 48 hours on $20M DHS "National Media Campaign" (LMD Agency) that Vought funded Sept 19; experts: likely violates publicity/propaganda appropriations limits.

DNC v. Trump (D.D.C. 1:26-cv-03506) filed over taxpayer-funded ads: alleges Trump directed Vought to "find a way" to fund them; OMB apportioned $20M of OBBBA CBP funds to line 6043 "Commemorative Events" Sept 19; the first ad aired Sept 23 and more than $2.5M was spent the first week.

Reuters (three sources) reports the White House has worked since April on plans for a Democratic Congress: executive actions on immigration, tariffs, housing costs and federal spending without congressional approval, with the counsel's office studying "what Trump can legally do on his own, where he could push the limits of his authority and how to defend those decisions in court." The Telegraph (via the Daily Beast, Nov 2) adds that Vought is reviewing what can be funded from money already appropriated and seeking grant-rule changes giving political appointees more control; agencies have submitted proposals and legal assessments. Trump: "I guess I'll become Mr. Veto."
tl.a: White House (Deputy Chief of Staff Miller; OMB Director Vought; White House Counsel Scharf)

tl.e: Roll Call: on Thursday Nov 12 Duffy and OMB Director Russ Vought sent appropriators a letter calling earlier ATC funds a "down-payment" and asking for $30.1 billion more, including $10.1 billion for air traffic control with $2 billion for "cloud computing and national airspace system telecommunications." Airways (citing Reuters): includes $7.2 billion for a common automation platform and controller workstations. Newsweek places the ask "Earlier Friday, before the outage."
tl.a: OMB Dir. Russ Vought; DOT Sec. Sean Duffy

tl.e: ODNI 2024 Annual Threat Assessment (unclassified; report dated Feb 2024, publicly released Mar 2024): "China remains the most active and persistent cyber threat to U.S. Government, private-sector, and critical infrastructure networks"; Mullin's Aug 24, 2026 letter cites it as a "recently declassified" record although it was an unclassified public report.

NIC memorandum "Foreign Threats to US Elections After Voting Ends in 2024" (Oct 2024; later declassified) assesses that "some U.S. adversaries—at a minimum China, Iran, and Russia…have the technical capability to access some U.S. election-related networks and systems"; Mullin cites it Aug 24, 2026 and the White House Transparency Task Force links it Aug 26, 2026.

HSI begins tracking voter-fraud arrests under program codes "VRO" and "VFR" from Jan 20, 2025: the ICE FOIA production shows tables headed "Voter Fraud Criminal/Administrative Arrests (VRO & VFR Program Codes) 1/20/2025 to Present" and "FY26 (last 7 days)" (tables withheld b7E); the definitions "Voter Fraud Alien" and "Voter Fraud Organizations" come from the HSI Mar 13, 2026 broadcast in the CNA v. Mullin record; RAVEn's Lead Tracking Tool lets "A lead creator ... attach program codes to leads, which are used to track investigative and enforcement efforts agency-wide."
Per Mullin, Georgia ran its state voter file through SAVE in 2026 and USCIS analysts identified more than 42,000 deceased registrants on Georgia's rolls.

Mullin's letter repeats a claim that in Feb 2026 a citizen found hundreds of ballots next to a dumpster at a commercial mailbox business in Renton, WA, plus 550 ERIC "Eligible but Unregistered" postcards sent there; he calls it "reckless use of DPPA-protected motor vehicle data."
tl.a: DHS Sec. Mullin (citing Skagit County Republican Party)

tl.e: Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar reported lead contender to run CISA (WH: "not accurate... at this time"); Jun 25 Mullin tells appropriators President met expected nominee: "get it built."
CNN interview: Mullin did not rule out ICE at midterm polls ("We would only be there if...").

As of July 2026, DHS had targeted at least 148 non-profits and churches conducting voter engagement, which plaintiffs say DHS "surveils, covertly infiltrates, and interrogates" (court's factual background in the CNA v. Mullin preliminary-injunction order, citing a partly sealed record, Dkt. 79-2 at 29-30, 99, 133).
Mullin publicly names Honey (Deputy Assistant Secretary, Elections Integrity, DHS PLCY) as leading review of state rolls.

Markey and Frost ask Mullin and Acting ICE Director David Venturella whether DHS keeps records of protest participants 'outside of the TSDS' and request the January ICE memo (CNN) directing capture of images, plates and information on 'agitators, protestors'.

White House roundup quotes officials and allies: Landry "hacking 220 million U.S. voter files"; Rep. Riley Moore "The CCP stole 220 million"; Sen. Lummis "2020 data breach by China"; Rep. Tenney "China attempted to manufacture fake ballots"; CIA Dir. Ratcliffe cites CIA Venezuela reporting and his 2021 ICA dissent; Mullin "over 250,000 potential non-citizens"; Michigan Speaker Hall thanks Trump for "directing FBI Director Patel to reopen" the Muskegon investigation.

Mullin to reporters (as quoted by The Hill): "your voter registration list needs to be scrubbed"; "I will tell you if the states choose not to participate — we will make sure that we make those states a priority to look at who voted in their states and hold the election officials accountable"; "Before and after the election, we will scrub all election records looking for illegal aliens and those who are ineligible to vote"; renews plans to withhold grant money from states that don't use SAVE.

EPIC v. Mullin filed (S.D. Cal.): face recognition, LPRs and other tech used to identify and retaliate against observers; DHS removed its 2023 face-recognition policy from its website without rulemaking.
tl.a: EPIC; Nicole Cleland; Jacquelyn Ivey; Anna Walker

tl.e: NPR reports the CLEAR database could be the source behind Mullin's 250,000-noncitizen figure (unproven)

USCIS generates TECS records on people flagged in its voter-eligibility matching (target lists initiated Aug 2026), as found in the CNA v. Mullin preliminary-injunction order citing the whistleblower disclosure.
NPR: Mullin says DHS will release voter analyses during early voting and while votes are counted; "maximum pressure"; fines/penalties/imprisonment for officials.

Tense CISA election-security call: Fontes "They don't work with us, they work against us"; Simon "states are almost entirely on their own"; Mullin reportedly vowed to withhold funds from states not implementing administration proposals. ProPublica: the August video call, a few weeks after the speech, was many officials' first meeting with acting CISA Director Nick Andersen; he said DHS was preparing an election plan and blamed lapses on the fall 2025 shutdown; Fontes: "I told him I didn't trust him" (R).

Chronology: Aug 21 FDNS personnel redirected to Unlawful Voter Initiative; Aug 25 FDNS voter reviews begin; late Aug ICE adds unlawful-voting question to booking intake (Oct 1 directive: ask admitters mail vs in-person); Aug 27 FDNS Tactical Operations social-media analytics solicitation; Aug 31 HSI "Public Voter Data and Handling" RFI. The CNA v. Mullin PI order (ECF 87, Oct 21, pp.1-2, citing ECF 10-7 at 11-13, 198-202, 336) describes the DHS "Unlawful Voter Initiative": USCIS personnel generate target lists for investigation for improper voting, initiated in August, and coordinate with HSI field offices to investigate them "through interrogations" (D, court's description). The government's opposition (ECF 46 p.37, Sept 28) quotes plaintiffs' Aug 21, 2026 start date for the "Voter Eligibility Matching Policy" and the TECS records under it without disputing it (D).

DHS Secretary Mullin writes the White House Transparency Task Force (letter dated Aug 24, 2026) that voting machines with China-made parts "introduce significant security risks": ES&S, Hart and Dominion (over 80% of the market) have "acknowledged that their voting machines have parts made in China," and tampered components could allow "synchronized attacks across multiple machines and jurisdictions"; he cites vendors' 2020 testimony, the "recently declassified" 2024 ODNI Annual Threat Assessment and an Oct 2024 NIC memorandum, not any exploitation; says "I have directed the Department of Homeland Security to prioritize election security," that DHS is doing rolling production and declassification review for the task force (some documents "cannot be released at this time"), and that full DHS grants require "random post-election manual counts of paper ballots." The task force posts it with an open-source supplement Aug 26.

The Aug 24 Mullin letter to the White House Transparency Task Force, as hosted by Just the News (file "08.20.2026 WHTF Letter  Commerce S1 SIGNED.pdf"), carries Word document properties Author and dc:creator "Disalvo, Karen", created 2026-08-24 16:44 ET in Microsoft Word for Microsoft 365 (read with pdfinfo, Nov 15). The White House copy (whitehouse.gov DHS-Election-Integrity-Memoranda.zip, with the Task Force's "Open Source Supplements" sheet dated Aug 26) has the same text with the document properties removed. Democracy Docket first reported the metadata (Aug 28; R).
tl.a: DHS Sec. Markwayne Mullin; DHS senior adviser Karen DiSalvo; White House Government Transparency Task Force; Just the News

tl.e: The White House (Government) Transparency Task Force releases, with the DHS Election Integrity Memoranda zip, an open-source supplement headed "Pursuant to Presidential Memorandum 'Promoting Government Transparency and Accountability'" linking the 2024 ODNI Annual Threat Assessment, the 2024 NIC memorandum "Foreign Threats to US Elections After Voting Ends in 2024," the 2020 House Administration vendor hearing, and a 2020 ES&S CEO op-ed calling for paper-ballot backups; the zip confirms Mullin's Aug 24 letter and the HSGP hand-count condition word for word.

Mullin tells reporters (Tuesday, Sept 1) DHS could be at polling places if there is "a threat to that polling place or we're serving a warrant on someone ... if we're serving a warrant we will be where we need to be," and gives a third exception: reports of specific undocumented immigrants at a location could be a reason to deploy. A subsequent DHS statement added that "ICE is not planning operations targeting polling locations" (per the Sept 4 House Homeland minority letter; an unnamed DHS official had used the same line Jul 31, Wisconsin Examiner). This departs from the Feb 2026 Heather Honey statement "There will be no ICE presence at polling locations."
Todd Blanche is confirmed as Attorney General "earlier this month" per Mullin's Sept 2, 2026 letter (exact confirmation date not stated; he was Acting AG through at least Aug 2026).

DHS Secretary Mullin writes Attorney General Blanche (Sept 2, 2026, on its face; scanned on whitehouse.gov as AG-Letter-S1-Signed.pdf), congratulating him on his confirmation "earlier this month" and, invoking DHS's Sector Risk Management Agency role for election infrastructure, informing him of "prior referrals" DHS made to DOJ "during my predecessor's tenure" (Noem); it makes no new requests and asks DOJ to "review these referrals." Referral 1: whether voting systems that count from barcodes or QR codes comply with HAVA Title III's voter-verifiable paper record and manual-audit requirement, 52 U.S.C. 21081(a)(2)(B); it cites EO 14248 and the CISA report in the White House "Vulnerabilities-in-Electronic-Voting-and-Ballot-Counting-Systems.zip" (p.4: hackers "could change the votes encoded in the barcode"). Referral 2: legality under the DPPA (18 U.S.C. 2721-2725) of states sharing motor-vehicle and voter data with ERIC and, via ERIC, with CEIR; DHS and DOJ met on it in Sept 2025. The letter asserts the ERIC model contract requires MVA data every 60 days and bars sending records indicating non-citizenship; cites a 2022 Colorado mailer to ~30,000 noncitizens, a 2026 Georgia SAVE run finding >42,000 deceased registrants, and a Feb 2026 Renton, WA ballots-by-dumpster claim (sourced to the Skagit County GOP); quotes the ERIC founder on Democratic targeting; and closes "as we support the President's America First agenda." It does not mention recounts and does not ask DOJ to investigate whether election nonprofits "improperly obtained" data in those words (earlier NOTUS/NYT summaries, R).
House Homeland Security Committee minority letter (Sept 4, 2026, pp.1-3) challenges Mullin's Sept 1 rationale (a threat or a warrant) for DHS presence at polling places.

Sens. Padilla and Schumer make public a USCIS whistleblower disclosure on the "Unlawful Voter Initiative" (Senate letter dated Sept 13, enclosing the Sept 8 disclosure letter; Padilla floor statement Sept 14). On the floor Padilla says he and Schumer wrote Mullin and USCIS Director Edlow demanding the program be halted and unreliable law-enforcement records deleted. The disclosure (hundreds of FDNS staff diverted, short training, "supplemental magic," ~40 subjects/day, raw data including "a lot of U.S. citizens," TECS records leading to HSI/FBI referral) is entered in the Congressional Record Sept 14 (S4641). Follow-ups: 16 senators ask DHS OIG to investigate; a 34-senator letter (incl. Kaine, Sept 28) combines the program, FEMA conditions and the TECS-to-HSI path. The CNA v. Mullin PI order (ECF 87 p.4) later recites from the disclosure that TECS records "can be used against [an individual] in any interaction they may have with the federal government" and that USCIS has created TECS records for U.S. citizens.
tl.a: Sens. Padilla and Schumer; USCIS whistleblower

tl.e: Lawfare links to Just the News and the Daily Signal for the text of Mullin's Aug 24 voting-machine letter.

In Hilton v. Mullin, No. 2:26-cv-00092-JAW (D. Me.), the government's motion to dismiss (ECF 117) says Agent J.C. documented plaintiff Carlyn Williams's name and vehicle in HSI's "Internal Case Management ('ICM') system," "which led to the March 2026 border stop referenced in the FAC" (n.13: he believed she was interfering with an arrest), and that J.C. documented subject records on 8 individuals he believed posed potential threats; no watchlist nomination (nn.12-13).

California Nurses Ass'n v. Mullin (N.D. Cal. 4:26-cv-10680) filed: challenges voter-matching and field operations incl. home visits questioning eligibility, intimidation of voter-assistance groups; PI hearing Oct 19.
tl.a: California Nurses Ass'n, NNU, City and County of San Francisco, Santa Clara County, Voto Latino (v. DHS, USCIS, ICE, CBP and officials)

tl.e: HSI "Enforcement Stats FY26 (last 7 days)": "Voter Fraud Cases Initiated: 869 1,163 (+497)."

On Fox News (Kayleigh McEnany, a Saturday, most likely Sept 19) Mullin says "We have 1,620 cases moving right now that are under investigation," 151 arrests, and "300,000 we're looking into and that list grows every single day"; he gave the same figures on CNN earlier that week. AP later reported 160 arrests.

CISA releases "2026 Election Infrastructure Security Plan: Securing the Next 250" (Mullin "tasked CISA" with it in July): 10 regional directors as election-security advisers; CISA "coordinates closely with ... the FBI" on insider threats and calls the temporary workforce's insider risk "a structural feature of election administration"; CISA, DHS I&A and FBI route federal threat reporting to fusion centers and "through them" to election officials; an information-sharing platform on the FIFA World Cup model; VRDB logs retained "at least one year"; it says hackers "attempted to breach voter registration systems in all 50 states, with confirmed success in at least 20 states" (no country named; p.6, fn 4 = CISA web page "Vulnerabilities in Electronic Voting and Ballot-Counting Systems (2026)") and recommends "paper ballots that can be easily reviewed" and audits "before certifying" (p.5); the Plan contains no China/PRC, "human-readable," barcode or "not binding" wording (saved text searched in full). DHS release quotes Mullin: "Election security is national security ... will be implemented in full." The plan says seasonal and volunteer workers, contractors and vendors make insider threat structural and that foreign adversaries may "exploit insider access"; it reports 107 open-source election-related incidents in TRIPwire since Jan 1, 2022 (96 bomb threats) and, from 2022 to Aug 2026, 58 exercises, 53 C-IED trainings and 2,100+ physical security assessments (pp.7-8).
Minnesota indictments Sept 24 (ten defendants, HSI), announced Sept 30 (DOJ26-1119) by Blanche, Mullin, Rosen.

Supreme Court stays the June D.D.C. (Sooknanan) ruling that the revamped SAVE was unlawful, in DHS v. League of Women Voters, No. 26A308 (stay application filed Sept 8); states may use SAVE pending appeal. Reported: DHS said it kept using SSA data "to help determine whether illegal voting may have occurred" during the block; SAVE has run >65M voters and flagged 28,635; in Texas 21% of flagged voters were citizens; error rate not released (R). California SOS (PR26-121) says it will not use SAVE. The stay runs pending the D.C. Circuit appeal and any certiorari petition; Justices Jackson, Sotomayor and Kagan dissent (docket). The government's Sept 28 brief in CNA v. Mullin quotes the order: "individualized inquiries ... are permitted under federal law during this period" (slip 6), and the government is "likely to suffer irreparable harm" if ordered to stop sharing information on noncitizens on voter rolls (slip 5).

Senate Democrats' letter to Secretary Mullin warns against DHS election activities: "Taken together, these actions amount to an illegal attempt to federalize the administration of the upcoming midterm elections"; cites the FDNS whistleblower's account of an "Unlawful Voter Initiative" and the HSGP holdback.
tl.a: Sens. Peters, Padilla, Durbin, Schumer, Hassan, Blumenthal, Sanders and others

tl.e: Bartell declaration (CNA v. Mullin ECF 46-1): USCIS compares voter information from states, public and "other lawfully available data ... against DHS and commercial database holdings" (¶10); before the LWV order SAVE referred positive non-citizen matches to FDNS, and "Following the LWV order, SAVE stopped referring such information to FDNS," but FDNS kept using what SAVE had referred because it was by then held under the FDNS SORN (¶¶12-13); SAVE referrals were "only a small portion" of what FDNS reviewed (¶14); FDNS weighed "the possibility that in rare circumstances U.S. citizens might be incorrectly identified as aliens" and proceeded (¶17). Bartell says EO 14248 prompted FDNS to review noncitizens and naturalized citizens who may have voted before naturalization (para 9) and that FDNS "is not a SAVE User Agency" (n.1; para 15); FDNS's new Criminal Investigative Division is "not directly involved in the investigations into unlawful voting" (para 7); FDNS closes a review on derived/acquired citizenship or discrepancies except where data suggest voting or registration before naturalization (para 19).
tl.a: USCIS FDNS Assoc. Dir. Nicolas Bartell

tl.e: Government opposition in CNA v. Mullin (ECF 46) does not deny that TECS records are generated on matched voters but calls a TECS record a nonfinal "starting point" that "simply 'warrants further review'" (responding to plaintiffs' contention that "DHS's directive to generate TECS records flagging certain individuals for further scrutiny" is final agency action); says DHS used the "best data it had available" and interviews were "expressly designed to resolve the discrepancies"; as a fallback offers an injunction "akin to Paragraph 3.b." barring field operations against people DHS knows or should know are citizens, saying HSI filters already do that.

HSI declaration in CNA v. Mullin (ECF 46-2) says "USCIS transmits lists regarding aliens or USCs to HSI," HSI "will send to ERO to determine alienage," and "When potential inaccuracies were identified in the USCIS lists, DHS ... developed a new model for generating leads"; HSI does not interview everyone USCIS entered a TECS record for.
tl.a: HSI (Acting Deputy Assistant Director, CBFCC; name redacted)

tl.e: SEB resolution "Dominion Update Coordination": "the Federal government has deemed the voting systems to be 'critical infrastructure' and the Dominion systems are 'protected computers' within the meaning of 18 U.S.C. sec. 1030(e) such that the knowing transmission of information over a Dominion system that is compromised could impair the integrity of data"; forensic images of EMS and ICC hard drives to be "provided to the State Election Board, DHS and the US Department of Justice (DOJ) ... for examination, review, or investigation"; directs Mills to assist DHS and DOJ "pursuant to their letter of September 2, 2026" on QR codes (HAVA) and ERIC/CEIR data sharing (DPPA, NVRA). Mills's Sept 30 letters to Mullin and Blanche ask DOJ to set a six-month deadline, compel patching with forensic backups first, and "preserve all such records under federal supervision."
tl.a: Georgia State Election Board (member Carolyn Roddy; executive director James Mills)

tl.e: DHS admits Americans may be watchlisted by mistake (Reason Sept 30); Palantir ICM records auto-shared to CBP TECS as lookouts (Maine litigation; Wired); HSI agent declaration in CNA v. Mullin: DHS "developed a new model for generating leads for HSI's unlawful voting investigations."

Hilton v. Mullin (D. Me.) filings: ECF 129 plaintiffs' response on First Amendment discovery privilege (Oct 1); ECF 132-40 Hilton and 132-42 Pantos supplemental declarations (Oct 2); ECF 142, 142-5, 142-10 (Oct 9); ECF 145 (signed Oct 9, filed Oct 13). ECF 129 (plaintiffs) says the government seeks community Signal chats and the names of people who identified federal employees and vehicles, and that the record shows at least one HSI agent in Maine planned to infiltrate a community group. ECF 145 opposes defendants' motions to seal (ECF 119, 137) agent names, Signal-chat content, ICM/TECS information, the OCTD operations order (PI Ex. 29), a briefing deck (Ex. 30) and a roster (Ex. 45).

Plaintiffs file their PI motion in redacted public form (ECF 132; unredacted version ECF 101-1 under seal), alleging use of HSI ICM and CBP TECS to create records on people observing immigration enforcement (deposition testimony); ECF 145 (Oct 13) later asks for public filing of the unredacted motion.
Senators' letter to Mullin demands evidence for noncitizen claims, the "Unlawful Voter Initiative," and rescission of HSGP election conditions (IBs 569, 569a).

CNA v. Mullin ECF 67 grants record completion for safeguard documents; ECF 71 (Oct 13) describes Nov 2025 email, Aug 2026 FAQs, Sept 2026 email instructing naturalization/passport/travel checks. ECF 67 (Judge Martinez-Olguin) requires FDNS documents on "safeguards intended to reduce the risk" of erroneous referral under the "Unlawful Voter Initiative Policy" and vacates the Oct 6 hearing.
Newly unsealed filings in the Maine observers case (Hilton v. Mullin) include agent deposition excerpts; other depositions remain sealed.
Ed Martin (Bolling interview): Mullin concluded machines are "compromised."

CNN and others report on the Oct 1 ICE FOIA release (Democracy Forward v. DHS): HSI ingested 50.6M DOJ-sourced voter records and 48.4M records "obtained by DAS Heather Honey through independent sources" (CNA v. Mullin ECF 87 gives 48.2M); data sent to iLab "for secondary enrichment and identification of high-value targets"; some records pending "entry into ELITE" (all D, FOIA); HSI reviewed "150+" voter-registration organizations (reporter's sum of component counts), considered undercover agents, and shared status updates with the White House from July (R, CNN). Palantir: "Voter roll data has never been integrated into ELITE" (R).

Plaintiffs' opposition to the motion to dismiss (Hilton v. Mullin ECF 142) argues the ICM and TECS records about Williams and her vehicle "have already led to Williams's (and Pantos's) detention once and [redacted], at least through January 2027" (citing CBP 30(b)(6) Dep. 146:7-147:10); each observer's ICM record carries a designation redacted in the public copy; and defendants "agreed to conduct only very limited database searches, excluding many of the databases discussed in the FAC" (n.37) (arguments, not findings). The brief also says ICE's Rule 30(b)(6) witness testified that threatening observers with a "domestic terrorist" designation was an appropriate "deescalation" technique consistent with DHS policy, and that no training on the 2019 DHS First Amendment memo was identified (pp.5-9, 15, 20).

Acting DAG McCotter sends letters (Oct 13) to California SoS Shirley Weber and LA County Registrar Dean Logan with a list of people DOJ "believes are likely noncitizens" who were mailed ballots, giving 48 hours (noon Oct 15) to verify; they are to "segregate not cancel" those mail ballots, send no new ballots and pause signature verification and tabulation, or DOJ "will seek emergency relief"; the letters cite 18 U.S.C. 611 and Norwood v. Harrison and ask the officials to work with DHS. HSI Assistant Director McLoughlin helps deliver the list (just over 20,000 names) to DOJ and the USAO (C.D. Cal.), and an HSI special agent serves the demand letter and the list on an encrypted drive at the LA County Registrar-Recorder's Norwalk office, handing it to the receptionist (Dkt 62-3 para 24, Ex. A, D). Per the order (D): on Oct 13 DOJ "hand-delivered a letter and password-protected thumb drive" to Logan containing PII of "over 20,000 individuals," while Weber was "emailed the same requests with a 48-hour deadline without an accompanying list" (ECF 149 pp.3-4, Compl. Ex. C; Weber Oct 15 letter p.2: "despite failing to send the list ... to my office, you demand that we request transmittal"). Instructions per the order: review the list within 48 hours, (1) segregate VBM ballots of non-confirmed citizens, (2) withhold unsent ballots, (3) not verify signatures or tabulate until citizenship is confirmed (Compl. Ex. D). LA County says it would not open the drive. DOJ release 26-196 gave the >20,000 count; our Oct 17 notes add that the password was on a sticky note (not in the order; R) and that DHS earlier claimed 190,000; Mullin called it a "preliminary analysis."
DHS S&T "Securing the World Cup" counter-drone named Innovation of the Year; Mullin (Jul 21): nearly 2,000 drones brought down.
Current-case safeguards production describing restricted supplemental material.

Defendants file the safeguards supplement to the administrative record in Cal. Nurses v. Mullin (ECF 71, Oct 13; exhibit ECF 73-1 sealed) and move to seal the supplemental AR (Dkt 74) as containing "detailed internal procedures, operational safeguards, and investigative methodologies that USCIS [FDNS] personnel employ when investigating unlawful voting"; the court grants sealing Oct 21 (ECF 87 pp.5, 17-18).
Democracy Defenders Fund files a Hatch Act complaint against Mullin, Edlow and Blanche over the Omar search.

Defendants reply ISO motion to dismiss (ECF 149); plaintiffs file PI reply with deposition excerpts of D.L., ICE 30(b)(6), J.C., J.R., S.C. and exhibits 68-83, under seal motion (ECF 148, 150); plaintiffs move for oral argument (ECF 151).
At PI hearing judge called requested relief "amorphous," signaled unlikely PI on APA claims, took VRA claims under advisement.

The CNA v. Mullin preliminary-injunction order finds that DHS data include 48.2 million records received "through independent sources" plus DOJ's voter-roll data, and that DHS "enriches" data through iLab, "using unknown artificial intelligence tools to ingest data from various systems and create a compiled list of individual profiles." The order also recites 50.6M records from DOJ (official rolls or, for non-sharing states, "unreliable commercial versions"), USCIS told to treat DHS source data as "presumptively valid," a 40-subject surge quota (~12 minutes per person), 1,586 leads to 24 HSI field offices from 2,290 records, and review of naturalized citizens for pre-naturalization voting.
tl.a: N.D. Cal. (CNA v. Mullin PI order)

tl.e: Judge Martínez-Olguín (California Nurses Ass'n v. Mullin, ECF 87) bars DHS election-related field operations and interviews involving people agents know, suspect or "should reasonably know or suspect" are citizens, including operations "based wholly on TECS records" from the matching, in nine states (CA, CT, GA, MO, NV, NY, PA, WA, WI); calls the target list "voluminous and unreliable" and finds likely voter intimidation under VRA §11(b) (APA and right-to-vote claims not reached); DHS's stated intent to target only noncitizens "does not cure" the reasonable fear. Stayed to 5 p.m. Oct 23; $100 bond due 5 p.m. Oct 22; runs only to 8 p.m. Nov 3 "or when polling places close." Only CNA/NNU have standing (associational, VRA sec. 11(b) intimidation of voter assistance and mobilization); the local governments and Voto Latino lack standing; sec. 11(b) carries an implied private right of action and reaches federal officials (pp.7-17).
Plaintiffs post the $100 bond in CNA v. Mullin (ECF 88); no stay motion or appeal as of Oct 22, 4:47 p.m.

CNA v. Mullin order takes effect 5 p.m. Oct 23 (runs to 8 p.m. Nov 3): (a) no elections-related field operations or interviews in nine states involving persons the enjoined parties know, suspect, or should reasonably know or suspect are U.S. citizens; (b) no elections-related field operations "based wholly on TECS records generated from the Voter Eligibility Matching Policy" against such persons (reading (b) as a subset of (a) is I). Court: "There is no federal database containing citizenship status of U.S. residents." DHS: "We have no plans to question or investigate people we believe to be U.S. citizens" (the court applies an objective standard, not DHS's belief); no stay request was reported by then.

CISA releases strategy "CISA 2030: Defend, Harden, Prevail" (cover Oct 2026; press release Oct 26): implements the President's Cyber Strategy for America (Mar 2026), the National Resilience Strategy (Jun 2026) and EO 14239; moves "from passive defense to an aggressive, anticipatory stance"; "deprioritize threat-agnostic, all-hazards approaches"; "integrate intelligence" pipeline with the IC; "maintain and analyze infrastructure data"; NS/EP communications lead; 60/180/365-day milestones. The word "election" does not appear in the strategy. Coverage (R): service review, "sharper focus" on critical-infrastructure threats; AI risks termed "super intelligence" (echoing the Sept 29 EO's terminology mandate); helps the White House build a "National Risk Register."
tl.a: CISA (Acting Dir. Nick Andersen; DHS Sec. Mullin foreword)

tl.e: DOJ files a notice of appeal to the Ninth Circuit from the CNA v. Mullin preliminary injunction (Dkt. 89, Oct 26), four days after plaintiffs posted the bond (Dkt. 88, Oct 22); named defendants include Edlow, Homan, Mullin, Salisbury, Scott and Venturella.
DOJ files an ex parte application to stay the CNA v. Mullin preliminary injunction pending appeal, with a Declaration of James C. Harris (Dkt 90); plaintiffs oppose the same day (Dkt 91).

At a CISA all-hands, Mullin says DHS will hold a post-election "debrief" to weigh changes to voting systems to improve voter trust in outcomes, and that DHS is not trying to "suppress" votes; scope unstated.

DHS release "Dozens of Illegal Aliens Arrested In Nationwide Voter Fraud Crackdown": ICE "has arrested dozens of individuals in connection with alleged voter fraud and election-related offenses"; it lists 13 examples, two described as having "illegally voted in the 2026 election," with alleged votes ranging from 1992 to 2026, each framed by criminal history; it says the government is "investigating alleged violations" by "aliens who admitted to voting."
