Mullin: "American elections are for Americans only." No total, no charges count, and no states given for most examples.

At a CISA all-hands, per an anonymous CISA official, Mullin said he would hold a post-election "debrief," that DHS was not seeking to "suppress" votes, and that he would weigh whether system changes were needed to improve voter trust; scope and who conducts it unclear. (R, Nextgov; Politico first)
Ninth Circuit denies DOJ's stay of the CNA v. Mullin injunction barring DHS election-related field operations in nine states; government "had not carried its burden."
Mullin tells Newsmax noncitizens on voter rolls "top 300,000" (headline; full text not retrieved).

Mullin says DHS sent DOJ a "large case" involving multiple people in the Omar probe; a DOJ filing refers to Omar and "other individuals"; more than a dozen grand-jury subpoenas in Minnesota; no charges.

CNN: Mullin says "Our job is to make sure that it's a legal ballot and it's counted" and "to make sure there's not vulnerabilities where bad actors can get into the system and change the vote," alleging past vulnerabilities without evidence; DHS stood up a last-minute online threat-intelligence platform and CISA an information-sharing tool that officials trust less than past channels.

DOJ stay motion (ECF 33, Nov 1, pp.13-19): Section 11(b) "does not apply to the federal government" (citing Judge Tung's dissental in CNA v. Mullin: "person" does not include the sovereign; "It is nonsensical that the Attorney General would sue the United States on behalf of the United States"); 11(b)'s definition of "vote" "presupposes a lawful vote," so it "protects those who aid qualified voters"; an "accurate statement of federal criminal law" cannot be "intimidation" at all; "the Elections Clause in no way limits or applies to the executive branch"; prosecution decisions get "a presumption of regularity." Democracy Docket reported the same argument Nov 2 (R).
tl.a: DOJ (SEIU v. DOJ, N.D. Cal. 3:26-cv-12800, ECF 33, stay motion; also argued in NAACP v. Blanche per reporting)

tl.e: On Election Day, Mullin tells Fox News: "ICE agents aren't going to be around polling places unless there's a threat"; "The only reason you'd see the Department of Homeland Security is if there's a threat"; "That's not their job. We're enforcing immigration." DHS also announces arrests of people from the Philippines, Italy, Finland, Algeria and Iraq for voting in 2024 (no names or totals reported); Mullin: "Only American citizens should be deciding American elections."

On Fox News on Election Day: "After this election we'll be gathering all the data, we'll be gathering the voting logs" ... "making sure that no illegals voted"; DHS "will be looking at the registers" and "all those that voted"; "it is still DHS' job to make sure that this was an election that was handled by the federal laws." No legal authority or method named. On X: "If you vote illegally, we will find you." ICE on X: "There will be no escape."

Thompson writes DHS Secretary Mullin demanding compliance with all document-preservation requirements and written assurance by Nov 11 "that Departmental records, documents, data, and information have not been and will not be destroyed, modified, removed, transferred, or otherwise rendered inaccessible"; the committee "intends to closely observe the compliance of the Department—and all its components"; responses to outstanding requests due by Dec 2; "In the 120th Congress, the Committee intends to address the Trump administration's assault on the rule of law" (D).
tl.a: House Homeland Security Democrats (Ranking Member Bennie Thompson, D-Miss.)

tl.e: Right-wing blogger Joe Hoft revives the FEC filing-system outage (Oct 27-28) as a "Midterm Early Voting Cyberattack" and asks "Where Is Secretary Mullin and Homeland Security?" The reporting he cites does not show a successful intrusion. (R)

DHS releases: at the White House Task Force (2028 Olympics) drone forum, Mullin: drones are "a serious and growing threat to public safety, critical infrastructure, and national security"; DHS is "building a lasting capability"; $250M FY27 Counter-UAS grants open to all 56 states and territories. In the Austin release: "No matter how much sanctuary politicians try to obstruct us, the patriots of ICE will keep doing their jobs." No election statement. (D)

DHS: ICE made more than 491,000 immigration arrests (nearly 475,000 administrative) and 483,200 deportations in FY26, records; 50,925 arrests in August. Mullin: "ICE has been unleashed to target and remove illegal aliens so that we can save American lives." DHS: "more than 3 million migrants have left the U.S."

American Oversight sued DHS and USCIS (D.D.C.) to force release of records on the USCIS "Unlawful Voter Initiative": six FOIA requests from Sept 16 for emails of Mullin, Deputy Secretary Troy Edgar, Senior Counselor Heather Honey and USCIS's Joseph Edlow using "unlawful voter," "voter fraud," "state voter," "FDNS enhancement"; Aug 21 training materials; review quotas; data sources and matching software; contacts with officials in 19 states and D.C. The suit cites a whistleblower disclosure (forwarded by Sens. Padilla and Schumer) that FDNS officers were reassigned to review voter rolls with quotas of five cases an hour and 40 a day.
tl.a: American Oversight; DHS; USCIS (Mullin, Edgar, Honey, Edlow)

tl.e: DHS release (sent Nov 16) on the Kinetic IV Counter-UAS Test Event, Stringtown, Okla., Nov 12: "This was the first time the event had been held at the Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma Emerging Aviation Technology Center (EATC), which had been championed by Secretary Mullin during his time in the U.S. Senate." Mullin: "DHS is working with state, local, tribal, and territorial partners, industry, and international allies to evaluate technologies that can address the evolving threat posed by unmanned systems," and "I am especially proud that the Choctaw Nation's Emerging Aviation Technology Center is hosting this critical work." Separately (Fox, Nov 15, via Epoch Times): "Absolutely not," "I'm not stockpiling," "This was a catastrophic outage that we were able to overcome."
tl.a: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin; DHS S&T Under Secretary Pedro Allende; Choctaw Nation Chief Gary Batton; Bahrain Ambassador Shaikh Abdulla bin Rashid Al Khalifa

tl.e: DHS S&T release on its Nov 3-13 counter-drone test at the Choctaw Nation's FAA-designated testbed, "championed by" Mullin as a senator; Mullin: "DHS is working with state, local, tribal, and territorial partners, industry, and international allies to evaluate technologies that can address the evolving threat posed by unmanned systems"; "I am especially proud that the Choctaw Nation's Emerging Aviation Technology Center is hosting this critical work."
tl.a: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin; DHS S&T (Under Secretary Pedro Allende)

tl.e: At a White House briefing on the FAA nationwide ground stop, Mullin: "There is no indication, and we have no reason to believe that as of right now that this was a threat to the United States"; "there was no indication, as of yet, that this was a nefarious act against us"; "We're not ruling out anything at this point"; "I don't want to say that this is a crisis, but it is"; on the FAA's new AI tool: "That's part of something that obviously, through CISA at DHS, we're taking a look." Fox: DHS "not ruling out" a cyberattack. Duffy reopened the airspace at 8:15 pm ET.
tl.a: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy

tl.e: DHS release of the White House FAA briefing quotes Mullin: "This is what the Department of Homeland Security is all about. This is why we were stood up, to have a continuity of government to bring all the resources together in an emergency like this... This is a national emergency. We have all of our assets, be it from DOW, to CISA, to all of our NOCs ... NSA is working with us." And: "The President has declared this a national emergency, and now we have to have Congress act and fund it." Also: "We have seen zero evidence that this is a cyberattack or an SI attack." No proclamation, executive order or National Emergencies Act notice published (White House presidential actions and Federal Register public inspection checked Nov 14).
tl.a: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin (with DOT Secretary Sean Duffy)

tl.e: SecurityWeek (citing Bloomberg): the FBI is examining whether a software update caused the FAA outage and does not think a cyberattack or criminal activity was behind it; Mullin says NSA, DoD, CISA and others were involved; "there's no chatter, we haven't seen any footprints ... we're not going to rule that out." No official root cause announced.
tl.a: FBI; NSA; Department of War; CISA

tl.e: DHS release (Nov 13; also quoted by Newsweek): "This is a national security risk because our air traffic control system is outdated and it hasn't been a priority from Congress. This is what happens when Congress kicks the can down the road."

Potter County Republican Party v. Benge (N.D. Tex. 2:26-cv-00215-Z, Kacsmaryk), ECF 72 First Amended Class Action Complaint (the Oct 27 original already sought the statewide defendant class, the pre-certification hand count, and cited Mullin's Aug 24 and Sept 2 letters; NEW in the amendment: plaintiff Alexander Hale, CISA's plan, results "corrected to match," and the reconciliation gaps). Keeps a defendant class of "similarly situated Texas county election officials" ("all the counties in Texas"); asks that "before final certification" all lawful paper ballots in the federal races of Nov 3 be hand counted and results "confirmed, or corrected to match the hand count"; a statewide hand count "in all precincts in Texas"; preservation of ballots, ballot images, cast vote records and chain-of-custody records. Opens: "Election security is national security." Relies on Mullin's Aug 24 letter (China-made parts, "synchronized attacks"), Mullin's Sept 2 letter to AG Blanche (QR/barcode ballots may not meet HAVA 52 U.S.C. 21081(a)(2)(B); EO 14248), CISA's 2026 Election Infrastructure Security Plan ("Securing the Next 250": "post-election manual audits ... before certifying"), and the Mar 20, 2026 router "National Security Determination." Cites preliminary-reconciliation gaps: Harris -4,085, Dallas -544, Randall -71, Lubbock +245. Potter County audit set for Nov 16; defense reply due Nov 17.
tl.a: Potter County Republican Party, Daniel Rogers, Alexander Hale (attys Jared Woodfill, Daniel Bates); defendant Christy Benge (Potter County Elections Administrator)

tl.e: Plaintiffs' response to the county's motion to dismiss (N.D. Tex. 2:26-cv-00215-Z, ECF 73): the injury is not "potential foreign actor and AI-assisted third-party interference" but unequal treatment, since each custodian decides whether a discrepancy leads to any further count; again quotes Mullin's Aug 24 letter ("election security is national security"; parts "manufactured by foreign adversaries introduce significant security risks"); says "DHS and FEMA have conditioned federal grant funds on a post-election manual audit of at least five percent of paper ballots"; the claims "challenge the procedure for counting and certifying in the face of vulnerabilities federal reviewers have found." County reply due Nov 17.
tl.a: Potter County Republican Party, Daniel Rogers, Alexander Hale (Woodfill Law Firm); Potter County Elections Administrator Christy Benge

tl.e: Mullin takes a government plane to the LSU-Texas football game in Baton Rouge less than 24 hours after the FAA ground stop, while travelers are still stranded; on Nov 17 he defends the use of the plane. (R, headlines: AP, CNN, USA Today, NY Post, Fox News, Nov 17)

Asked whether a bad actor could have flooded the Arkansas routers: "I don't believe in coincidences until I'm proven wrong. And right now, I'm being proved wrong"; "So is it a possibility? ... Possibly"; "with 98 percent certainty, that this was ... a 50-year-old system"; "use all 22 of our components to make sure that's not taking place. And if it did, we'd be honest with the American people and say, 'This is what's taken place, this is who did it, and this is who we're going after.'" On Iran: Trump and family "target number one"; drone threats "very aspirational, but we are well prepared inside the United States" (R, Daily Beast; Fox live blog).
tl.a: DHS Sec. Markwayne Mullin (Fox News, The Sunday Briefing, host Peter Doocy)

tl.e: Word-run comparison (8-word runs) of the Potter County complaints against the primary Aug 24 letter: ECF 1 reproduces 354 of the letter's 758 words, ECF 72 reproduces 374, including both ODNI quotes, the full China-parts paragraph and the footnote URLs. ECF 72 paras 1, 2 and 5 state the letter's sentences as the plaintiffs' own allegations without quotation marks ("Election security is national security. Electronic voting systems have one job..."; "States must trust but verify the results produced by the voting machines"), footnoted to the letter or to CISA's plan. ECF 1's "rogue artificial intelligence" paragraph (no source cited) is gone from ECF 72. Docket (CourtListener, 72 entries): no standalone preliminary-injunction motion filed after the Nov 4 order (ECF 50) and the Nov 6 extension request (ECF 58, citing "the loss of a second attorney"); intervention motions by DSCC/DCCC and Common Cause/LWV Texas/MOVE Texas/NAACP Texas undecided; ECF 43 (plaintiffs' certificate of interested persons) lists no financially interested persons and names "DSCC and DCCC" as the filer; the county's motion to dismiss (ECF 59/60/63, County Attorney C. Scott Brumley) calls the suit "statewide intervention into the process of certifying election results based on no more than theoretical possibility."
tl.a: Potter County Republican Party, Daniel Rogers, Alexander Hale (Woodfill Law Firm; Daniel Bates); DHS Sec. Mullin

tl.e: Mullin calls counter-drone his number one issue, says DHS saw more than 2,000 drones during the World Cup (700 confiscated), says "we're seeing new technologies that we're having a hard time defeating right now," and lists where he wants the same protection next: the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, critical infrastructure, high school football, parades, college and NFL games, "any mass gathering" (as reported by DroneXL). Same interview: "I don't think anybody's going to get fired over this. This was an issue with the equipment" (The Hill).
tl.a: DHS Sec. Markwayne Mullin (Fox News, The Sunday Briefing)

tl.e: On Fox's Hannity, Mullin says of the recent outages (FAA, Microsoft, banks): CISA told him "we're not seeing any traffic that would make us think that this is a cyberattack, they're all individually unrelated"; an unnamed tech source told him "I believe that it's the SI"; "it causes these systems to be over[run] that weren't designed to run as fast as the SI technology is today ... That kind of makes sense to me"; "the backup systems are overwhelmed by the new systems now." HuffPost reports he put his certainty there was no cyberattack at 98%. On Nov 17 CNBC headlined him: "We are not under attack."

On the FAA outage: "I believe that it's the SI" (superintelligence, relaying an unnamed tech-industry contact's theory about self-coding, self-fixing programs) and "with 98% certainty, we're not seeing a cyber attack." (R, Fortune, Nov 17)
tl.a: DHS Sec. Markwayne Mullin (Fox News, Hannity)

tl.e: Janelle King appointed to Georgia State Election Board.

ProPublica (Doug Bock Clark, Nov 13): recordings, board documents and EIN communications show board members and much of the professional staff working with EIN and allied groups; five sources say Mills worked closely with EIN members; at least three of eight staff attended EIN meetings; chair Fervier: "the Election Integrity Network has been having an undue influence on the State Election Board"; Fervier accused Mills of exceeding board authority by calling for DOJ and DHS to assess the state's voting machines.
tl.a: Georgia State Election Board (Executive Director James Mills; members Janice Johnston, Janelle King); Election Integrity Network (Cleta Mitchell)

tl.e: House Judiciary testimony urging Congress to enact the SAVE Act; no federal database proposal.
DHS associate chief of USCIS briefed Cleta Mitchell's Election Integrity Network on using SAVE to "aid in assuring that noncitizens are removed from our voter rolls."

Urged Commerce Sec. Lutnick to use regulatory authority (EO 13873 foreign-adversary supply chain; foreign-made parts) over voting machines before midterms: "impose mitigation or prohibition"; Ed Martin account of Oval meeting; Becker: "The commerce secretary has no authority."

Mitchell argues EO 13873 (May 2019 ICT supply-chain emergency) lets Commerce Sec. Lutnick require changes to Georgia voting software; Martin recounted Peters' White House meeting on his show (Democracy Docket); a transcribed Oct 6 appearance in project notes has him urging Commerce action (recording not linked, U).
Votebeat: Mitchell argues the 2019 EO 13873 emergency lets Commerce compel a partial hand count; Lindell: "The president needs to completely declare a national emergency."

Reported HSI workflow: state voter files and DOJ records (50.6M) plus ~48.4M records sourced via Heather Honey (FOIA figure; the CNA order gives 48.2M "through independent sources" and does not name her) -> HSI iLab matching/enrichment (Athena named; this production does not name RAVEn) -> leads -> HSI operations/organization reviews -> proposed ELITE entry (later reported not integrated); the Athena voter-matching pilot preceded the 2026 expansion; enriched records for 6 states awaiting ELITE.

Announced participation in pilot to improve SAVE with DHS, USCIS, DOGE (33 referrals to AG); Dec 9, 2025 Texas-DOJ MOU; Mar 25, 2026 meeting of TX SoS GC Adam Bitter with Heather Honey and USCIS; Apr 28 USCIS reply naming FDNS and SAVE leads; Nelson raised erroneous citizenship flags.
Heather Honey (who challenged 2020 results) appointed DHS deputy assistant secretary for election integrity.
Honey tells state officials DHS had not received/requested voter data; DHS contradicts same day (officials' Nov 18, 2025 letter).
Honey: "Any suggestion that ICE is going to be present at polling places is simply disinformation ... There will be no ICE presence at polling locations."

Heather Honey placed as Deputy Assistant Secretary, Election Integrity (new position); ICE records title her "ICE Senior Advisor, and Deputy Assistant Secretary, Election Integrity, DHS Policy Cyber, Infrastructure, Risk, & Resilience section" (May 20, 2026) and "Senior Advisor to the ICE Director and now also S1 Counselor" (Jun 5, 2026); weekly reports credit "DAS Heather Honey" with 48.4M records "through independent sources of information" (May 25/Jun 1). tl.e: Judge Carter DENIES DOJ's TRO application (Dkt 62) to make California and Los Angeles County segregate and not count the vote-by-mail ballots of ~20,000 people on the "October List" (ECF 149, 26 pp.). Holdings at the likelihood-of-success stage, not final merits: (1) the U.S. likely lacks Article III standing no "interference" with 18 U.S.C. 611 enforcement (DOJ is actively charging people; refusing to help is not impeding, US v. California, 921 F.3d 865), it cannot "spend its way into standing," and vote dilution is too speculative (Clapper, Lake v. Fontes); (2) no cause of action the Supremacy Clause creates none (Armstrong) and there is no equitable tradition of commandeering state election officials; (3) Section 611 does not preempt California election law no conflict, the Elections Clause leaves procedure to the states absent a clear congressional statement (Gregory v. Ashcroft; ITCA), and the theory raises Tenth Amendment anti-commandeering problems; (4) the relief would likely violate the NVRA 90-day bar (the October List is a "systematic" program like the data-match in Mi Familia Vota v. Fontes; "temporary segregation" has the same effect as removal: "a ballot segregated, in effect, would be a ballot removed," because neither DOJ which admits it cannot verify before Election Day, Compl. para 60 nor the counties can verify), VRA 52 U.S.C. 10307(a), and the Civil Rights Act materiality/different-standards provision 52 U.S.C. 10101(a)(2)(A) (procedure applied only to listed voters; A-number matching cannot reach U.S.-born citizens); (5) no irreparable harm the emergency is "solely due to its own neglect" (roll in hand May 8, Weber notified Jul 16, suit Oct 15); (6) equities: "the Court cannot conclude that Plaintiff's process is credible"; (7) Purcell bars relief; (8) the public interest favors voting rights and election staff. Disposition: "DENIES the Application" (p.26). The order appoints no special master and sets no hearing date, no PI schedule and no ruling on the motions to dismiss. DOJ files a notice of appeal of ECF 149 the same day (ECF 152). A CBS headline the same day read "Court dismisses DOJ's request" (the order is a TRO denial; the case stays open).
tl.a: Judge David O. Carter, C.D. Cal. (United States v. California, No. 2:26-cv-12025)

tl.e: Carter finds DOJ's list process not credible: DOJ withheld matching rules, confidence-threshold criteria and third-party details, disclosed LexisNexis only the night before the hearing, never explained the HSI "enrichment process," gave no error rates or benchmark validation, and never explained how ~190,000 became ~20,000; with Nevada's 15,903 -> 6,218 -> 185 -> zero record, "the Court cannot conclude that Plaintiff's process is credible." It also relies on the USCIS whistleblower report (County Opp. Ex. H: quota of 5/hour, 40/day, "only twelve minutes" per subject, IDs based "solely on DHS data that is unverified") and finds naturalized citizens most at risk.
tl.a: Judge David O. Carter, C.D. Cal.

Carter appoints Daniel B. Garrie as special master in US v. California, orders an expedited hearing on the motions to dismiss and DOJ's preliminary-injunction motion for Nov 13, 10 a.m., and orders all parties to file witness lists, including experts, on "the reliability of the October List and the methodology Plaintiff used to produce it" by Nov 6 (ECF 159). Intervenors oppose DOJ's Rule 62(d) application for an injunction pending appeal (ECF 160; DOJ application ECF 153).

Hearing on Los Angeles County Registrar Dean C. Logan's motion to dismiss DOJ's complaint in United States v. California (ECF 68, filed Oct 21) is set for Oct 30, 2026, at 8:30 AM before Judge Carter (per the ECF 68 docket text). The State defendants filed their own motion to dismiss the same day (ECF 65); Logan's ex parte application to expedite briefing and the hearing on the motions to dismiss (ECF 57) was joined by the State (ECF 61) and opposed by DOJ (ECF 72). ECF 149 (Oct 28) does not rule on the motions to dismiss; whether the Oct 30 setting stands is not shown on the docket through ECF 152 (U).
tl.a: Judge David O. Carter, C.D. Cal.

tl.e: U.S. v. California, 2:26-cv-12025, ECF 181, order closing case: "This lawsuit attempted to disrupt an ongoing election and create confusion and uncertainty for voters and election workers alike. The right to vote is sacred. So, too, is trust in our democracy." The Nov 13 hearing on "the validity of the government's list" is moot and vacated. (D)
tl.a: U.S. District Court, C.D. Cal. (Judge David O. Carter)

tl.e: Export-Import Bank IG Parisa Salehi fired.

DHS publishes modified SORN DHS/USCIS-004 SAVE (90 FR 48948-48955, FR Doc. 2025-19735, docket USCIS-2025-0337): adds U.S. citizens by birth; adds full/truncated SSN, U.S. passport number, driver's-license number and SSA-supplied data; adds record sources SSA-60-0058 (Numident), State STATE-05/-26/-39 and driver's-license agencies such as NLETS (DL search "not live at the time of publication"); clarifies voter verification and says it is "reinserting voter registration that was previously published in 76 FR 58525" as an administrative clarification; SSN case creation and the list processor were limited at first to web-browser users, and the list processor creates individual cases ("this is not batch processing"); a new oversight account type may view other user agencies' case data linked "by benefit type ... or by state"; new routine uses L (SSA and other authorized entities) and M (oversight/auditing) effective Dec 1, 2025; keeps routine use G (disclosure to law-enforcement agencies investigating violations of law) while stating SAVE information "is not to be used for administrative (non-criminal) immigration enforcement purposes." Prior version 85 FR 31798 (May 27, 2020); comments due Dec 1, 2025 (the SORN gives no comment count; the "9,361" in earlier notes needs a docket cite, U); exemptions "None." SSA published its companion Numident SORN modification Nov 12, 2025 (90 FR 50879; effective Dec 12, 2025).

SSA modifies Numident SORN 60-0058 (90 FR 50879, FR Doc 2025-19849, docket SSA-2025-0225; applicable on publication Nov 12, 2025; new routine uses effective Dec 12, 2025, comments invited to Dec 12): new routine use 49 lets SSA give DHS "the citizenship and immigration status, lawful or unlawful, of any individual pursuant to 8 U.S.C. 1373(a)" with no agreement, purpose or volume limit written into it; new routine use 50 to Treasury Do Not Pay; existing routine use 2 deleted; signed by Matthew Ramsey (Head of Privacy and Disclosure Policy). The notice never names SAVE or voter verification except existing routine use 36 (HAVA SSN-4 checks for chief election officials). The SORN states no comment count (an earlier "21,298 comments" figure is unsupported, U).
Homan said federal officials were gathering records and reviewing Rep. Ilhan Omar's immigration history.
Comer letter to Omar's husband requests business/financial records citing Minnesota social-services fraud.
Vance said DOJ was examining whether Rep. Omar committed immigration fraud and would prosecute if evidence found.
Vance again addresses the Omar investigation as task-force matter; says DOJ is looking at it
Undercover HSI agent found outside Rep. Omar's Minnesota town hall in a vehicle.
OCC voted 5-1 in Sept to recommend dismissal of allegations related to Omar's financial disclosures; Pirro probe opened Oct 13 (husband's eStCru LLC, Rose Lake Capital).

Clustered noncitizen-voting charge announcements: Sept 30 (10 in MN), Oct 5 (16), Oct 8 (S.D. Ala.), Oct 12 (16 in NM, PA, AL, MO, ID, NJ, OH, HI, KY), Oct 13 (Alabama arrests); Omar residential search Oct 12 (same day).

HSI agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar's D.C. home in a pre-dawn raid in an immigration-fraud investigation, reportedly after Public Integrity Section consultation and Blanche approval (Fox/Reuters, R; AP does not say who approved), while Minnesota voting is underway; family subpoenas follow. AP: HSI searched the D.C. home on Monday Oct 12; DOJ: a "judicially authorized search warrant," "part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation"; Omar calls it an attempt "to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement." The warrant is sealed (Oct 15 row).
DOJ packaged 16 election-crime defendants in one announcement, some previously announced; Omar search approved by Blanche after Public Integrity review (JM 9-85.500 followed in form).
Pirro opens a disclosure probe into Omar; Vance denies advance notice of the search.
AP reports investigators seized Rep. Ilhan Omar's phone in the citizenship-papers probe and that her relatives, including her sister, received grand-jury subpoenas about immigration paperwork.
Reuters reports the search warrant for Rep. Omar's home is sealed and that news organizations asked the court to unseal it; no affidavit or referral record is public.

NYT (relayed by Daily Wire, MEAWW): Omar's sister's phone was seized "earlier this year"; family texts helped obtain the Oct 12 warrant; Omar's phone, passport, notebooks and computers were seized; NY Post: a 2023 records search requested by a private activist found no proof of her father's naturalization.

DOJ opposes media motion to unseal the Omar search warrant: it "hasn't been fully executed"; "Unsealing everything now ... imperils the investigation"; DOJ "expects that the warrant will be fully executed in short order." No charges filed.

NYT (Londoño, Dahir): prosecutors charged a man who briefly served as Omar's bodyguard with lying under oath after a green-card interview that asked non-standard questions (whether he had "any interactions with any government officials or politicians"); his lawyer, Bruce Rivers, says prosecutors tried for months to turn him into an informant and told him the Omar investigation was "100 percent being run by 1600 Pennsylvania Ave." The case was assigned to the Minnesota USAO criminal chief and fraud/public corruption chief; DOJ dropped it in September and says it is "completely unrelated to any current investigations." The Omar probe also covers her financial dealings. Omar has denied wrongdoing.

Star Tribune (Jeff Day, Sarah Nelson): the Minnesota U.S. Attorney's Office investigated Omar for immigration fraud in Trump's first term and closed it without charges after deciding the deadline to prosecute had passed (three people familiar); prosecutors in Washington, D.C. now investigate her immigration history and finances without Minnesota's federal prosecutors; a D.C. grand jury has been hearing evidence; agents seized her phone, laptop, notebooks and passport Oct 12; family members including her sister subpoenaed. Emmer told Newsmax DOJ is reviewing "four different things," including her age at derivative citizenship. The paper cites a 2025 DOJ memo widening denaturalization to anyone posing an "ongoing threat"; no time limit on civil denaturalization. Omar's office: "an abusive fishing expedition driven by the president's political vendettas." Unsealing hearing Nov 17 (D.D.C. 1:26-mc-00144).
tl.a: Rep. Ilhan Omar; DOJ (D.C. prosecutors, U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro); U.S. Attorney's Office for Minnesota; Rep. Tom Emmer; HSI

tl.e: Watson writes AAG Harmeet Dhillon about DOJ's proposed voter-list Memorandum of Understanding; after consulting 12 other states, Mississippi raises concerns about federal and state roles under the NVRA and HAVA, the information DOJ would give states on "potential list-maintenance issues," state review including a proposed 45-day requirement, and references to the Civil Rights Act of 1960; asks to meet Dec 15 (D).
tl.a: Mississippi Secretary of State; DOJ Civil Rights Division

tl.e: LaRose letter to Dhillon re USCIS verification, seeking more DOJ resources (CRT-0003126-3127).
Told Just the News her review of state rolls found "tens of thousands of noncitizens" who could vote and "hundreds of thousands of dead or departed residents."

Supreme Court decides Watson v. RNC, No. 24-1260 (5-4): federal law fixes when ballots must be cast and state law sets when they must be received, so Mississippi may count mail ballots received up to five business days after Election Day; Kavanaugh joined the Alito dissent in part. The Solicitor General's Feb 2026 amicus brief (Dhillon, Civil Rights Division, on the brief) supported the RNC, arguing "all votes must have been received on election day to count." Trump calls it a "tremendous loss" that makes the SAVE America Act "more important than ever" (Daily Signal, R).

DOJ's Civil Rights Division writes election offices in all 50 states and D.C. that any election officer "who knowingly retains noncitizens" could face criminal liability, citing 52 U.S.C. 20511 (Jul 7, 2026; same day as the rulings in and).

NAACP v. Dhillon (D.D.C. 1:26-cv-03461-SLS): FOIA suit filed Oct 2 seeking DOJ election-monitor records; emergency motion Oct 5 for monitor authority, locations, criteria, training and any ICE use; DOJ opposes the TRO Oct 13 (R).
DOJ: 112 people charged in 20 states in seven weeks, 155 total; "literally thousands" of potential noncitizen-voting cases under investigation

Joint status report in NAACP v. Dhillon (D.D.C. 1:26-cv-03461, ECF 28), the FOIA suit over DOJ's election monitors. DOJ quotes the Neff declaration ¶6: "while monitoring, the monitors will not be acting as 'law enforcement personnel,' a 'law enforcement officer,' or a 'law enforcement agent' as commonly understood." DOJ says it "has not yet finished identifying all locations for deploying monitors," will not commit to a date before Election Day, and that publishing them could put monitors at risk. NAACP says DOJ counsel conceded criminal prosecutors and investigators from DOJ criminal components and U.S. Attorneys' offices will serve; that the declaration names DEA, BOP and ATF personnel without the "no agents" language used for the FBI and ICE, and does not mention the U.S. Marshals; and that an ATF employee is among the monitors. DOJ's searches returned 18,993 and 7,842 potentially responsive records; it says none can be produced before Nov 3.
tl.a: DOJ Civil Rights Division (Neff declaration); NAACP

tl.e: DOJ press release 26-1310, "DOJ To Monitor Elections in All 50 States for First Time": "approximately 1,000 election monitors and observers deployed, and, for the first time, in all 50 states"; "Monitors will include personnel from the Division, other DOJ divisions/components, U.S. Attorney's Offices and federal observers from the Office of Personnel Management"; Dhillon: "pursuing transparency for elections in an assertive and nondiscriminatory manner." The release describes the Criminal Section as enforcing statutes against "voter intimidation and voter suppression based on race, color, national origin, or religion," and tells the public to report violence or intimidation to local police first. It lists the counties and cities (e.g., Texas: Bexar, Dallas, Harris, Waller, Blanco, Bowie, Nueces; Georgia: Cobb, DeKalb, Fulton, Gwinnett, Chatham, Bibb; Michigan: Lansing, E. Lansing, Grand Rapids, Flint, Detroit, Hamtramck, Warren, Dearborn).
Dhillon resigns as Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights, two days after the election; she signed the July 50-state voter-roll demands (R).

Jason Reding Quiñones, the Miami U.S. Attorney whose office ran the "grand conspiracy" investigation of Trump's opponents, resigns; CNN counts three DOJ officials gone since the midterms (with Dhillon) (R).
tl.a: DOJ / U.S. Attorney S.D. Fla. Jason Reding Quiñones

tl.e: Jon Eisenberg of DOJ's National Security Division resigns; Blanche on X says he was "strengthening our nation's ability to address threats, both foreign and domestic." CBS: "DOJ exodus continues" (with Dhillon and Reding Quiñones) (R).

Lawyers Defending American Democracy files a professional-ethics complaint against Dhillon, acting Deputy Assistant AG Robert Keenan and acting Voting Section chief Eric Neff, alleging they kept pursuing the voter-roll suits against 30 states and D.C. after courts "repeatedly rejected" the theory (LDAD: DOJ had lost all 27 cases ruled on as of Oct 23). The complaint quotes Neff telling a Rhode Island court DOJ would run the records against DHS's SAVE.
tl.a: Lawyers Defending American Democracy; Harmeet Dhillon; Robert Keenan; Eric Neff

tl.e: LDAD files an ethics complaint with the State Bar of California against Dhillon, Keenan and Neff over DOJ's voter-record suits, alleging claims that are "frivolous, involve legal and factual misrepresentations, and undermine public confidence in our elections" (allegations).
tl.a: Lawyers Defending American Democracy; Harmeet Dhillon, Robert Keenan, Eric Neff (DOJ Civil Rights Division)

tl.e: Craig Trainor, HUD's fair-housing assistant secretary and a former AFPI staffer, is tapped as acting Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights, replacing Harmeet Dhillon, according to an administration official. (R)

OPLA legal broadcast "Preserving and Protecting the Integrity of American Elections" (Dec 29, 2025, 5:56 PM, to OPLA Regional and Division personnel): "ICE has begun coordinating with CBP, USCIS, and the Department of Justice" to identify aliens who registered or voted; noncitizens who voted can be removed without conviction and without proof they knew it was illegal, including where the evidence is "insufficient to support a criminal prosecution."
tl.a: ICE OPLA (Deputy PLA Adam V. Loiacono; Acting Deputy PLA Nelson Perez)

tl.e: Sessions introduces bipartisan Stop Identity Fraud and Identity Theft Act to 'strengthen the Nation's digital identity verification infrastructure' (bill number not given).

House Oversight Subcommittee on Government Operations holds "Emerging Fraud Threats and the Evolving Fraud Landscape" (Serial No. 119-70; Sessions chair; 2:03-3:58 p.m.; most majority members absent for an Administration Middle East briefing). Witnesses: Jordan Burris (Socure Vice President and Head of Public Sector Strategy; former Chief of Staff, White House Office of the Federal CIO), Marisol Cruz Cain (GAO IT & Cybersecurity), David Maimon (SentiLink, Georgia State) and Jay Stanley (ACLU, minority witness). Burris says "identity should be considered critical infrastructure" and that Socure is a Login.gov vendor after competing against 17 others (document verification, facial biometric comparison, device and fraud models); Sessions proposes that Login.gov identity-verification failures (who failed, where, how) be studied and moved "to the organization we talked about this morning, to Pandemic Response Accountability Committee (PRAC)," says Congress will make PRAC's data effort permanent, and asks whether it is "fair game to go back and run people back through" benefit programs because "a lot of people that presently are receiving government benefits might not be exactly as we thought they were," and whether AI flags (e.g., "74 people at your home address") can trigger review. Rep. Randall enters the Wired article "A DOGE Affiliate Is Now in Charge of the US Government ID Platform"; Ranking Member Mfume says DOGE used an SSA identity database to mark people. GAO: Login.gov meets NIST IAL2 after a remote identity-proofing pilot, agencies lack visibility into why users fail, 100M+ users, 50+ agencies, 500 applications incl. state and local. Industry witnesses (SentiLink, Socure) urge "real-time cross-agency data matching," holding payments via an expanded Do Not Pay, continuous identity re-verification and "historical signals" from commercial data.
tl.a: House Oversight Subcommittee on Government Operations

tl.e: FEC Form 13: HPE gave the Trump Vance Inaugural Committee $250,000 on Jan 23, 2025, a week before DOJ sued to block its Juniper purchase. The same report lists Verizon ($1,000,000, Dec 19, 2024), AT&T ($1,000,000) and IBM ($750,000). (D)
tl.a: Hewlett Packard Enterprise; Verizon; AT&T; IBM; Trump Vance Inaugural Committee

tl.e: Ueland's nominee financial disclosure (OGE 278e, signed Mar 18, 2025): Ueland Consulting LLC, President/CEO since 3/2021, $570,420 in consulting fees; sources paying more than $5,000 for his services: American Hospital Association, APTS, Humana Health, Commonwealth Fund, the Heritage Foundation and the America First Policy Institute. Heritage Foundation Visiting Fellow 3/2023-12/2024 ($55,000 fellowship income to the LLC); volunteer, Trump Vance 2025 Transition, Inc. 11/2024-1/2025; advisory board, Center for Constitutional Liberty, Benedictine College 7/2022-1/2025; USCIRF commissioner 5/2022-1/2025.
tl.a: Eric Ueland (OMB nominee, Deputy Director for Management)

tl.e: Vance: "We have activated a major interagency task force" on fraud, two months before the order that formally creates it; at the same briefing he says DOJ will create a new associate attorney general position dedicated to fraud and cites 1,500 subpoenas and 100 indictments.
Vance, as fraud task-force chair, refers Minnesota Gov. Walz and AG Ellison to DOJ's fraud division (post Monday night, Jun 8, 2026; reported Jun 9); outcome unknown.
Task-force press conference on visa fraud; green-card program suspensions and nine university investigations.

Headline (Carolina Coast Online): "Boliek signs Vance fraud pledge, expands NC watchdog efforts." Boliek already sits in DOJ's Southeast Fraud Enforcement Partnership (Jul 30) and his office took a $1.9M Special Attorneys award.
tl.a: North Carolina State Auditor Dave Boliek

tl.e: NSA names Tim Kosiba (ex-TAO requirements & targeting) deputy director.

Richfield, MN observer Nicole Cleland is addressed by name by an agent who cites facial recognition (Jan 10); her Global Entry/TSA PreCheck is revoked Jan 13 (reason as quoted in project notes not confirmed in KSTP; agency per KSTP).

A DOJ privacy lawyer tries to narrow voter-roll sharing to specific individuals (Feb 12, 2026 warning that raw voter data to DHS carries "far too much unnecessary legal risk"); a Mar 4 draft still allows transfer; the final, short DOJ-DHS letter, signed by the acting ICE director about two days later, is broader and drops the proposed party-affiliation redaction.

Per a USCIS whistleblower disclosure released by Sens. Padilla and Schumer (packet ~37 pp; Democracy Defenders Fund cover letter Sept 8): on Aug 21 FDNS officers are told to "stop everything" and watch a 1h45m training ("there will be U.S. citizens in this population"); Aug 24 FDNS is reorganized under HQ control; Aug 25 reviews begin, target Sept 12; quota 5 an hour, 40 a day (~12 minutes each), "up to hundreds of thousands" across 50 states. Inputs: state voter-lookup websites (an internal site links all 50 state portals; VA, FL and Massachusetts flagged "(Attestation)," i.e. users attest to being the voter allegation, R), SAVE (source label "IRIS"; other labels "DOJDHS," "ICE"), Accurint and Thomson Reuters CLEAR, and SSA and State passport data in batch queries; officers are told to create TECS records on "unlawful voters" that can trigger HSI referral; agency counsel called the searches "open-source research."

Bipartisan amicus brief (199 House, 47 Senate, 15 former House members; Schumer and Jeffries listed; no party affiliations given) in No. 26A305 (USPS v. California; Trump v. League of Women Voters of Massachusetts) urges the Supreme Court to deny a stay of the D. Mass. injunction against the USPS mail-ballot Final Rule: the Elections and Postal Clauses give the Executive no power; no statute delegates it; the Rule conflicts with HAVA, NVRA, UOCAVA and Title 39. Filing day not on the copy read (stay denied Sept 14).
tl.a: 261 current and former members of Congress

tl.e: Officers must create a TECS record on anyone judged an "unlawful voter," 40 reviews/day quota; warned "there will be U.S. citizens in this population." USCIS: its criminal unit "was not directly involved" (D, declaration).
tl.a: USCIS whistleblower (via Sens. Padilla/Schumer, posted Sept 13-14)

tl.e: Press conference demanding DHS stop; cites whistleblower claims of daily case quotas.
Two suits seek to keep armed federal agents away from polls: one led by the NAACP (Sept 18) and one by the DSCC, DCCC, DGA, Schumer and Jeffries against DHS, ICE and the FBI (Sept 23)
Polling Place Policy suit vs DHS, ICE, FBI (armed agents at polls, VRA 11(b), APA); separate NAACP-led suit Sept 18.

DSCC v. Trump, D.D.C. 1:26-cv-3674 (filed Oct 20, 2026 by Schumer, Jeffries, DSCC, DCCC, DGA and Nevada Democrats): Elections Clause, separation of powers, anti-commandeering, VRA §11(b); DOJ's roll push began summer 2025; 27 courts dismissed DOJ roll suits; portal "imminent." DOJ says "election integrity is a top priority"; the White House calls it "decisive lawful action" (Axios Oct 21, R).
tl.a: Schumer, Jeffries, DSCC, DCCC, DGA, NV Dems

tl.e: DOJ tells the court its letters to states about alleged noncitizen voters "have no independent legal effect" and "do not themselves change any voter's registration status, withhold a ballot, or alter ballot tabulation"; argues plaintiffs lack standing.

Colom leads Hyde-Smith by 1,138 late Nov 4 with nearly 3,600 mail ballots outstanding and, per unconfirmed reports, upwards of 18,000 affidavit ballots statewide still to be cured (cure deadline Nov 10; counties certify Nov 13); Schumer reportedly sending DSCC legal resources (R).
Ordered four Virginia state agencies (State Police, Corrections) to terminate 287(g) agreements; on Jan 17 rescinded Youngkin EO; 22 sheriffs still participate.

Treasury publishes a Notice of Proposed Designation (91 FR 5990, Feb 10, 2026, FR Doc. 2026-02630, docket TREAS-DO-2026-0034; signed Gary Grippo, Acting Fiscal Assistant Secretary) to add SSA's Numident to the Do Not Pay Working System: Numident "will be used solely for the purpose of verifying the name, SSN, and date of birth" of people receiving federally funded payments or awards under health or income maintenance programs (e.g., Social Security retirement, Medicare, Medicaid, including federally funded state-administered programs); SSA returns only numerical match codes, not other Numident data; SSA discloses under routine use 17 of SORN 60-0058 (90 FR 50879, Nov 12, 2025); comments due Feb 25, 2026; a final designation would be a separate Federal Register notice (whether it was issued: U). Do Not Pay system access uses PIV credentials, Login.gov and ID.me; Do Not Pay estimates $1.5-4.5 billion a year in at-risk payments addressed.
William Kirk appointed PRAC chair (from Mar 1, 2026, succeeding Horowitz).
SBA IG William Kirk (political appointee) became PRAC chair, succeeding Michael Horowitz; he holds SBA IG, PRAC chair and SBA PRAC seat.

SBA OIG Management Advisory Report 26-15 (Sept 24, 2026, IG Kirk to Administrator Loeffler; review period Apr 3, 2025-Apr 30, 2026) finds a fraud-detection AI pilot missing from SBA's public AI inventory: it targets PPP, EIDL, RRF, SVOG and disaster loans plus 8(a) contracts "and the awarding contracting officer for indications of possible collusion"; SBA managers said it "did not qualify as high impact, even though the model would be potentially flagging loans as fraudulent" (OMB presumes such fraud detection high impact); 34 inventoried uses, 19 with PII, none designated high impact; report cites SBA release 26-29 suspending 111,620 California borrowers (Feb 6, 2026); SBA (Deputy CIO, Sept 15) agrees to all six recommendations with Sept 30, 2026 targets.
tl.a: SBA OIG (IG William W. Kirk, also PRAC chair)

tl.e: Hearing on major-event information sharing: NFCA's Mike Sena describes a Super Bowl LX info-sharing environment "that combined... a common public safety Geographic Information System (GIS) analysis tool with a commonly used chat, video, and file sharing technology"; federal DHS/FBI systems "not fully interoperable with state and local platforms"; Sena opposes the Fourth Amendment Is Not For Sale Act.

Horowitz: losing PACE would cost oversight "an invaluable resource"; Dodaro: permanent center "would be ready and there when emergencies occur"; GAO-22-105715 recommended a permanent analytics center.
Blanche at CPAC: "Why is there an objection to sending ICE to polling stations?"

Acting AG memo "Creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division" (Apr 7, 2026): creates NFED and an NFDC "dedicated to identifying fraud across taxpayer-funded programs"; within 14 days the Criminal Division and EOUSA report ongoing investigations and "significant events ... expected to occur within the next 90 days" (complaints, indictments, pleas, trials, sentencings); each U.S. Attorney's Office details a prosecutor to NFED within 21 days; partners include EO 14395 task-force members; grants to "enable state and local prosecutors"; the memo does not mention elections.
DOJ anti-fraud press conference: "elected officials need to support the Justice Department in stopping this fraud."

Trump v. IRS settlement creates $1.776B "anti-weaponization" fund (May 18); Blanche says DOJ not moving forward (Jun 1-2); Judge Brinkema blocks fund indefinitely (Jun 12); Judge Williams voids settlement as collusive (~Jul).
20+ senators ask Blanche why the Election Crimes Manual was removed

Sen. Schmitt and five other Republican senators write Acting AG Blanche and AAG McDonald (DOJ fraud leadership) asking, by Aug 24, 2026, for the "Status of voter-roll cleanups, specific election-fraud prosecutions, immigration-related fraud schemes," state coordination on removing ineligible voters, federal-state information-sharing barriers, sanctuary jurisdictions, and proposals to make the National Fraud Enforcement Division permanent with "enhanced data-sharing."

At his Senate confirmation hearing, asked by Sen. John Kennedy about his relationship with Trump, Blanche says "I'm his lawyer," then corrects himself to "was his lawyer"; says Trump never asked him to do anything illegal and he "Absolutely not" would if asked. Confirmed 50-49 in August (Newsweek, Aug 16).
Letters (Aug 19, Aug 27, Sept 1) to AG Blanche on DOJ plan to deploy up to 1,000 election monitors; Wyoming GOP officials raised alarms over "aggressive" monitors in August primary.

Wall Street Journal: Pulte "also looked at" the mortgage records of Todd Blanche, then deputy attorney general, after they clashed over the mortgage cases; sources say Pulte was "trying to collect information on Blanche and others." Pulte's lawyer calls that false; DOJ says Blanche has one mortgage. (R)

Sens. Padilla, Durbin and Whitehouse ask AG Blanche (cc FBI Director Patel) to pledge DOJ will not seize ballots, materials or voting equipment before certification and to disclose any seizure plans (answer due Oct 29); Padilla separately secured FBI Director Patel's commitment that the FBI will not seize ballots or machines ahead of the midterms.
NAACP v. Blanche, 1:26-cv-03626, challenges deployment of criminal prosecutors and law-enforcement personnel as election monitors.
AG Blanche won't rule out DOJ intervening in state certification in "some doomsday scenario," while saying he is "not trying to not have an election certified." A statement, not an action
Blanche says lawsuits against other states like the California ballot suit could follow

AG Blanche (CBS Face the Nation; CNN State of the Union, Oct 25): the Alaska suit is "guardrails" and "not saying don't certify," but if a court finds a result "decided because of confusion and not the will of the voters," "we do not think the states should certify"; DOJ wants a procedure "if there is litigation brought by others after the election" and is "doing our own research"; he won't discuss communications with the President; on CNN: "Oh, stop it!... We're not laying any groundwork." (Headlines that "there could be a crime" are unverified.)

Written answer due to Sens. Padilla, Durbin and Whitehouse on committing not to remove ballots, materials or equipment from state custody before certification; no public answer reported as of Oct 30 morning.

In NAACP v. Blanche (D.D.C. 1:26-cv-03626-RBW, ECF 22, Nov 2), Judge Walton denies the TRO on DOJ poll monitors without prejudice (finding "a reasonable voter would not be intimidated" by plain-clothes non-law-enforcement volunteers, and that his view "would differ" if DOJ planned to send officers with arrest authority) but orders DOJ to comply with its counsel's concession that monitors "are indeed administrative or clerical personnel and not law enforcement officials, will not be in uniform or display any other insignia ... will not be armed with a firearm, and will not have the power to effectuate arrests," plus the Neff Decl. ¶12 limits (business casual; no visible federal insignia; "not talk with any voter inside the polling place"; talk to voters outside only after they vote; carry credentials). Plaintiffs may file a notice of any Nov 3 violation and the court "will take immediate action." DOJ status report due 7:00 a.m. Nov 3 on how it confirmed no monitor is a law enforcement official with arrest power.

DOJ status report in NAACP v. Blanche (D.D.C. 1:26-cv-03626-RBW, ECF 24, filed Nov 3) under Walton's order: "Though there is no prohibition on the use of sworn law enforcement officers as civil rights election monitors, CRT undertook reasonable efforts to avoid using sworn officers"; FBI and DHS personnel excluded; after weeks of consultation "DEA prohibited sworn officers from serving as election monitors"; review with ATF and U.S. Marshals leadership "resulted in the removal of several sworn law enforcement officers from the volunteer monitoring pool"; Bureau of Prisons employees, who "have legal authority to make limited arrests" (18 U.S.C. 3050), remain, because "It is inconceivable that anything could happen at a polling place where a BOP employee serving in a monitoring capacity would be authorized to make an arrest"; "No additional sworn law enforcement officers were identified" on Nov 2.
tl.a: DOJ (Civil Division for CRT); D.D.C. (Judge Walton)

tl.e: On Fox News (MacCallum), on Alaska: "There's a scenario where the incumbent, Senator Sullivan, could lose"; "If it's clear that voters were confused, and again, that's why you need to preserve these ballots"; authorities could "look at the individual ballots."

Watson statement: about 3,600 mail ballots left plus an "unknown" number of affidavit ballots; "Counties have 10 days from the date of the election to submit their certified results to our office, which is November 13." AP (Wed night, 96%): Colom leads Hyde-Smith by 1,138. Alaska: Peltola leads Dan Sullivan by 637 with nearly a quarter uncounted; ranked-choice tabulation Nov 18 (R, Al Jazeera/AP Nov 5). Democracy Docket: if Hyde-Smith loses narrowly the GOP "will likely mount a legal effort to challenge ballots" and DOJ "could be joined"; Blanche vows to keep "fighting tooth and nail" on Alaska (R).
tl.a: Mississippi Secretary of State Watson; Alaska Division of Elections

tl.e: Washington Post: DOJ braces for congressional subpoenas after the Democratic sweep (likely topics: the Trump IRS settlement, Epstein files, pardons, the Comey prosecution); the story cites an OLC executive-privilege opinion released earlier this year. Blanche on Fox: "It's so disgusting to see them not even wait before the week is out." (R)

At Jackson City Hall, across from the Hinds County Courthouse where Mississippi affidavit voters had to cure by 5 p.m. Nov 10, Blanche, Gov. Reeves, AG Fitch and U.S. Marshals Director Serralta announce more than $63M for Jackson under DOJ's Model Cities Initiative (one of four cities; ~$300M total), including a "Real-Time Public Safety Center" and a "Sky-to-Street Public Safety Network utilizing unmanned aircraft systems." Blanche on Fox, the third time in two days: "We cannot let the rhetoric turn from just honest debate to actual criminal conduct"; "There's been so much vile rhetoric coming out of the incoming congressmen and senators, and also from organizations that are outside"; "you cannot threaten." Bloomberg Law: Singh urges U.S. attorneys onto a "wartime footing," warns of more removals, and asks each office to name 2-3 AUSAs who can move to priority cases in other districts.

DOJ has not rescinded the California grand-jury subpoenas.

Breitbart and The Western Journal report Attorney General Blanche is the latest cabinet official moved onto a military base; The Times counts four cabinet members living on bases amid Iranian threats.

Incoming Democrats are "acting like prosecutors ... They're acting like they're going to cut subpoenas left and right"; "We're going to be there, and we're not going to just stand by willingly." Per Tampa Free Press, Blanche said the administration has been reaching out to private companies and supporters, advising them not to fold under congressional pressure, and alleged outside legal groups are working with incoming House Democrats to target officials including the chief of staff.

tl.e: Joint DOJ-Commerce statement on the Megaspeed investigation (press release 26-1365): Commerce opened the probe in 2024; in May 2025 investigators asked Nvidia for records; in June 2025 Nvidia put Megaspeed on its "no sell" list and BIS agents, with Singaporean officials, did an end-use check and interviewed CEO Alice Huang; DOJ then took the criminal lead. "While we don't typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting." Credits "the Department of Commerce under Secretary Howard Lutnick."
tl.a: Department of Commerce; Department of Justice; Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick; Attorney General Todd Blanche

tl.e: DHS IG Cuffari reports "systematic obstruction" (March 2026).
Cuffari told Congress DHS had "systematically obstructed" 11 OIG reviews, including the Butler probe.

Under a federal grand jury subpoena, the Arizona Senate gives the FBI dozens of servers and drives holding 200+ terabytes from the 2021 Maricopa "audit" (Cyber Ninjas reports, county electronic records, images of county election systems, possibly ballot images and voter files); Petersen: "The FBI has the records"; Maricopa says it got no subpoena; the AZ SOS weighs legal options to protect voter data; AG Mayes calls it "weaponization."

tl.e: Arizona's U.S. Attorney announces an investigation of three voter-registration groups (Stand Indivisible Arizona, Worker Power, When We Count) based on undercover videos by a Heritage-affiliated site, refers it to the FBI, and writes Maricopa Recorder Heap and Secretary of State Fontes asking them to review registrations the groups submitted. The videographer says "absolutely no voter registrations were submitted."
tl.a: USAO D. Ariz. (U.S. Attorney Timothy Courchaine); FBI

tl.e: DOJ letter describes arrangement: DOJ gives DHS public voter rolls; DHS "enrich[es]" them with DHS records so they can be run through SAVE.

Sworn declaration in NAACP FOIA suit (D.D.C.): "There will be no Federal Bureau of Investigation or U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement employees, much less agents, serving as monitors"; DOJ "is not using sworn law enforcement officers with arrest powers as monitors in a law enforcement capacity." Says nothing about seizure of ballots or equipment.
tl.a: DOJ Civil Rights Division Voting Section (acting chief Eric Neff)

tl.e: InDepthNH reports acting Voting Section chief Eric Neff told New Hampshire Secretary of State David Scanlan in September that he is under criminal investigation for refusing NH's unredacted voter list, with a demand to preserve evidence ("spoliation ... civil and criminal sanctions"). DOJ's civil suit lost in June; appeal pending (1st Cir. 26-1783).
tl.a: DOJ Voting Section chief Eric Neff; NH SoS David Scanlan

tl.e: FDNS becomes a designated law-enforcement entity as of Oct 6, 2025 (stated in the Bartell declaration n.1, which cites no rule); a new FDNS Criminal Investigative Division employs special agents.

On or around May 8, 2026, USCIS FDNS receives the California voter roll from HSI for noncitizen review (the roll was purchased from the California Secretary of State, buyer not named, and given to HSI by a DHS senior counselor about Mar 19; it holds name, address and DOB, no SSN or ID numbers); FDNS then enhances it with Accurint data. FDNS Associate Director Bartell says USCIS "receives state voter rolls or information on state voter rolls from DHS," analyzes them and refers matches to HSI. HSI's Eric McLoughlin says HSI "initially reviewed the list of millions of registered voters in California" and "formatted and delivered" it without changing data, and describes HSI's statewide role as "data intake (including obtaining bona fide voter rolls), preparation, enrichment, quality review, and routing of leads" (Dkt. 62-3 paras 11, 14, 20). The roll reflects voter registration as of Aug 2025.

A USCIS FDNS list of 20,930 "likely noncitizen" California registrants, built from the purchased California roll (buyer not named) enriched with LexisNexis Accurint and scored by FDNS into confidence levels, is given to HSI and delivered to California on Oct 13, 2026 (Bartell: "My understanding is that list was delivered to California on October 13, 2026"); the process "is distinct from" SAVE, which "was not utilized" (para 14); USCIS later found about 189 records with "minor data discrepancies" on the list and alerted HSI (n.1).

DOJ files its original ex parte application for a TRO and order to show cause to block counting of ~20,000 mail ballots (Oct 19; lodged as attachments to an application to exceed page limits, ECF 22, 22-1, 22-2, with the McLoughlin and Bartell declarations), asking for relief by Nov 3; the case is assigned to Judge Holcomb Oct 20 (ECF 34) and has no hearing or ruling before the Oct 21 transfer.

Oct 21 in United States v. California: the case is transferred to Judge Carter as related to 2:25-cv-09149 (docket ECF 46; ECF 149 cites "Dkt. 44," which on the docket is Judge Holcomb's standing order); DOJ refiles its emergency ex parte TRO application as to noncitizen vote-by-mail ballots (ECF 62; Bartell, McLoughlin and Hamill declarations) after leave to exceed the word limit (ECF 53) and says Los Angeles County had processed more than 331,000 mail ballots since Oct 11 (R); the Court "immediately" sets an Oct 27, 1:00 PM hearing (ECF 64); "a few minutes before 9:00 p.m." DOJ asks for a ruling by noon Oct 22 (ECF 67); on Oct 22 DOJ files a notice of appeal claiming "constructive denial" (ECF 74).

Democracy Docket reports how DHS found ~20,000 California names is 'a mystery' (unnamed third-party platform; roll source not stated); four days later Bartell Decl. #2 (ECF 107-2, Oct 26) names the roll as purchased from the CA SOS and the platform as LexisNexis Accurint.

Bartell Declaration #2 (US v. California ECF 107-2, executed and filed Oct 26 for the Oct 27 TRO hearing before Judge Carter) lays out the FDNS pipeline: roll "purchased from the California Secretary of State and provided to HSI" (Ex. A; buyer not named; no SSNs), reaching HSI about Mar 19 from "a DHS senior counselor" (107-3 ¶5) and FDNS about May 8 (¶21); six fields sent to LexisNexis Accurint, which returns aliases, SSNs, DOBs, dates of death, phones and addresses (¶15); paired with A-numbers (¶16); name+DOB+SSN queries to State and SSA, none without an SSN (¶17); FDNS confidence levels (¶18) and two-level manual review (¶19); refined list to HSI (¶22), which "continued to further refine the data with federal law enforcement systems" (62-3 ¶23); 20,930 names delivered to California Oct 13, ~189 with "minor data discrepancies" (n.1); 17,000+ more under review, "most ... will end up being referred to HSI" (¶24). Bartell: FDNS Associate Director since July 2026, senior counselor to the USCIS Director Sept 2025-Jul 2026, Acting AD Apr-Jul 2026. USCIS receives records "on a rolling basis before the election date" (para 24). A companion Bartell declaration on LA County's 200-name sample (Dkt 107-1, same day) says USCIS found 51 people on the DHS list whose California roll entry gives a U.S. birthplace, but that none matched to the sample were U.S.-born per USCIS records; re-review found 4 who "might have a claim to U.S. citizenship" and 1 deceased (paras 6-13, n.1, Ex. C).
tl.a: USCIS FDNS Assoc. Dir. Nicolas Bartell / DOJ

tl.e: DOJ status report: "Defendants confirm that they are in compliance with this Order." Senior officials named as responsible: Brian Hawkins, Intergovernmental Liaison, DOJ; Brendan Shelley, Deputy Assistant Director for the Cross Border Financial Crimes Center, HSI, ICE; Larry DeNayer, Associate Director, Immigration Records and Identity Services Directorate, USCIS. Restates carve-outs: SAVE inquiries and "prosecuting violations of federal law."
FIFA after-action: Intelligence Coordination Center of 400+ staff, ~100 intel reports, ~300,000 background checks; "put everybody under one roof."

Patel writes to the "White House Task Force on Government Transparency" that the Maricopa incident "mentioned in the Election 2020 cyber intrusion logs kept by U.S. intelligence agencies" was "fully investigated," that the suspect scraped 633,000 voter files from the county's "registrar servers," including 930 "sensitive, nonpublic" records, and that the USAO, AZ AG, Maricopa County Attorney and Pinal County Attorney "All declined"; he encloses the opening and closing ECs and the suspect's FD-302.

The Task Force releases the Maricopa packet (Patel letter, FBI opening/closing ECs and FD-302 with file names dated "8.5.26," plus an "Election Day Log"); the White House posts that a "self-described hacker" stole 633,000 voter files "but the Biden DOJ declined to charge him"; an unnamed official briefed reporters Aug 5; The Federalist reports the White House "requested information about the prosecutors who declined."
tl.a: White House Government Transparency Task Force

tl.e: At a September Senate Judiciary hearing, asked about federal law enforcement at polling places, Patel says: "I don't know that we can't legally do it."

Patel testifies that the FBI-overseen NSPM-7 Joint Mission Center has personnel from 10 agencies, integrates intelligence, operational support and financial analysis against "domestic terrorism and organized political violence," with 200+ arrests and 250+ indictments/complaints; separately says the FBI will "thoroughly investigate election crimes" as the midterms approach.

Superseding indictment unsealed against Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, Mohsen Mohajeri and Mohammad Ali al-Hassani for supporting Kata'ib Hizballah and Iran's IRGC in "nearly 20 attacks and attempted attacks throughout Europe and the United States" and a Sept 2026 plot at RAF Fairford. tl.a: DOJ National Security Division; FBI Director Kash Patel; S.D.N.Y. (U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald)

Duffy: Patel, the DNI and the Defense Department joined a call over concern of a cyberattack from another country; no chatter found; "It wasn't a foreign actor." Cause: an L3Harris contractor's copper-to-fiber work at a remote site; routers flooded; "user error or installator error from L3Harris, or did they install a faulty router."

The FBI says it is helping the FAA and L3Harris examine the hardware, which stays with the network provider. Duffy and other officials say they have ruled out a cyberattack or an AI-related cause. (R)

22 states, D.C. and Pennsylvania's governor (summarized as "24 states and D.C.") sue in Massachusetts over EO 14399's citizenship-list and mail-ballot provisions (California v. Trump, No. 1:26-cv-11581, Judge Talwani); the League of Women Voters of Massachusetts brings a parallel challenge (partially consolidated for briefing Apr 22). Lyons letter to Rep. Frost and 11 Democrats: ICE keeps no 'separate, standalone database' of protesters, but encounter information is kept 'as an official government record'; denies the eight code-named programs.
DOJ's $1.776B "anti-weaponization" fund: TRO denied (CREW), judge warns DOJ not to "play possum"; fund later indefinitely blocked/scrapped.

DOJ official sought access to Missouri voting machines.

Jul 22: HSI sends overdue "WAR and Voter Fraud Weekly," apologizing for delay "during the transition"; (A) CoS: "I shared with Director Venturella."

DHS (No. 1:26-cv-02624-BAH): 166 Bates-stamped pages (PDF 169 pp. incl. 3 cover pages; letter also refers to 164 released pages) of 808 pages processed, 642 withheld as non-responsive or duplicate, released in part under Exemptions 5, 6, 7(C), 7(E) and 7(F), answering requests dated July 27, 2026; custodians include Lyons, Wall, Feere, Bensman and Venturella; the cover letter asks that the documents not be shared with third parties.

Substack: "I found a second vote.gov and it's registered to the White House" (May 27); Jun 1 video with Wajahat Ali (NDS built/took over 45+ .gov sites outside normal privacy/procurement rules); Jun 10 "Trump Built A New Passport.gov Website" (passports.gov sign-in with no agency/privacy notice; auth/photo subdomains; Login.gov GitHub "proofing agent" change); BoingBoing May 27: 40 White House sites behind one private Cloudflare gate; reports NDS installed visitor-tracking on federal sites.

Release says Pulte will use intelligence post to look into "rigged elections," grouping James, Schiff and Cook.

Letter to acting DNI Pulte: the 50 U.S.C. 3371a(b) report on 2026 midterm election-security vulnerabilities and foreign threats was due May 7, 2026 and has not been provided; ODNI has given one staff-level briefing; the redacted 2024 election-threat assessment (ICA, Jan 21, 2025) has not been released; NIC analyst cuts. Calls the 2020 declassification push a "transparently partisan political exercise." (D)
Jay Clayton confirmed DNI 51–47 (Pulte acting <6 weeks); watch prompt corrected.

Jay Clayton is sworn in as Director of National Intelligence (Aug 3, 2026), ending Bill Pulte's acting tenure; as DNI he is responsible for the EO 13848 sec. 1(a) post-election assessment due ~Dec 18, 2026.

FHFA cuts its inspector general's budget by more than 60%; acting deputy IG James Hodge says it "will eliminate our capacity to effectively conduct criminal investigation of mortgage, bank, and other fraud schemes" (about 40 investigators). The IG is reportedly investigating Pulte. Its semiannual report says FHFA withheld records, so the IG was "unable to publish three reports." (R)

Reuters (Marisa Taylor, Chris Prentice), Oct 30: the FHFA OIG's semiannual report, sent to lawmakers Friday, says the agency obstructed its oversight and "called the obstruction 'unprecedented.'" FHFA "refused to provide records and information in response to the watchdog's requests during at least three separate evaluations." The OIG is "entitled to access 'all records,'" the report said; two weeks after an August "understanding," FHFA notified it of "drastically reducing" its funding: "The unprecedented and abrupt cuts will prevent OIG from conducting meaningful oversight of FHFA going forward." FHFA spokesperson: allegations incorrect, it has "readily produced" information; "FHFA is proud of its record of respecting the independence and role of the OIG." Reuters: first interference flag in at least a decade of these reports; staff told up to 80% could be cut.

tl.e: Hilton's sworn declaration states that on Jun 16, 2026, around 8 a.m., a vehicle she believed to be an ICE vehicle, which she had followed for about 45 minutes, drove to the street she used to live on and stopped for at least 20 seconds outside the address on her driver's license (where her father still lived), the driver waving at her "jokingly," before driving away (declarant's account; allegation, not a finding).

Task force initially charged with uncovering election fraud releases records from past investigations of Trump (Mueller, Smith probes); allies cite them for a Florida DOJ effort to indict investigators.
tl.a: White House fraud task force (John Solomon)

tl.e: At a July 2026 panel: not concerned about IG firings; "the executive branch should have some say over their policies and their procedures."
Education IG nominee Semann withdrawn Sept 17; Mark Priebe nominated week of Sept 28; Rene Rocque acting again (Education OIG revolving door).

HSGAC nominations hearing, Nov 19, 9:30 a.m., SD-342. Panel I: Michael LoSapio (CISA Director), Eric M. Ueland (Comptroller General, GAO), Michael Chamberlain (Director, Office of Government Ethics), Robert Steffens (USPS Governor), Jeffrey Zisk (Postal Regulatory Commission), Mark Priebe (Education IG), Dennis Kirk (Interior IG). Memo dated Oct 13, released Nov 5 (press release 26-1319), creates the DOJ Super Intelligence Task Force (DOJ-SITF) under EO 14434, absorbing DOJ's AI Task Force. Members include the FBI, National Security Division, Criminal Division, National Fraud Enforcement Division, Civil Division, Antitrust and the Solicitor General. Components and U.S. Attorneys "should, from time to time at the request of the DOJ-SITF, notify the DOJ-SITF upon seeking to open an investigation" and "before seeking charges" in "matters involving SI"; it is DOJ's point of contact with the White House SI Force ("SI Force Chair Jay Clayton"). The memo cites "misuse of SI by foreign state and state-sponsored actors"; the release promises to guard against "malicious SI actors" and those "maliciously targeting American taxpayers, critical U.S. infrastructure." No definition of SI or "malicious SI actor"; elections not mentioned (D).
tl.a: DOJ (Attorney General's office; Associate AG Stanley Woodward, Associate Deputy AG Stephen Weiss)

tl.e: Judge refuses to enforce grand jury subpoena for Fulton County 2020 election-worker information ("the Court will not enforce it"; breadth "staggering").

NPR (via AlterNet, Nov 13): Santa Cruz County received a DOJ list of 81 suspected noncitizen registrants; "more than half are not registered in Santa Cruz County," "some names do not match any person currently registered or previously registered," and some birth dates "appearing well into the future like 2044." CEIR's David Becker expects congressional scrutiny of DHS's methodology; Loyola's Justin Levitt raises the Privacy Act notice question.

tl.e: Khanna letter to the President: no briefing offered on the China intelligence; hopes reports of "your potential intention to use China as a pretext for an executive order" are inaccurate.

A "100-Day Risk Mitigation Election Plan," subject "Proposed DHS/CISA Operational Guidance for the November Federal Election 2026" (dated Jul 22, 2026; no author named in the text), proposes six measures: ~900 of ~3,144 counties to "immediately terminate the use of BMDs"; GREEN/YELLOW/RED county triage with CISA "immediate technical intervention" for RED; "Insisting that the official count can only be certified after a full hand-count of every ballot" (later narrowed to federal contests); paper poll books with signature lines; logs preserved "through certification"; an "immediate CISA escalation channel for suspected compromise"; and DHS/FEMA treating the hand count as meeting the 5% manual-audit grant condition. Media Matters (R) attributes it to Peters, Parikh, Reynolds and Huff, reports a Jul 24 cover letter to CISA's acting director, Reynolds/Huff calls for a "national emergency," and Peters saying "CISA is not a forceful body." It also asks DHS/CISA to issue five deliverables at once (a Risk Mitigation Advisory, a BMD-to-hand-marked transition guide, a "Bank-Teller" hand-count manual, a paper poll book guide and a worker surge toolkit) and to classify counties GREEN/YELLOW/RED within days 1-7 with mandatory county reporting (secs. IX, XI).

tl.e: Peters takes election-conspiracy roadshow to Washington; reportedly met Trump; American Oversight opens investigation into her access to administration and federal election officials.

tl.e: IC report "PRC [redacted] Analysis on U.S. Voter Registration Information [redacted] from Multiple States, [redacted] Conduct U.S. Identity Matching and Public Opinion Analysis; 2019" (issuer masked; report date redacted; title year 2019) and its fuller "18 States" version: a PRC actor analyzed U.S. voter-registration data from 18 states, obtained by a redacted means, built from "Mid-term Elections" voter records (names, DOB, addresses, party, voting history, military affiliation, "election donation expenses," polling place) for "mining PII," U.S.-person identity matching and General Election opinion analysis; visible states AK, CT, FL, MD, NY, DC, NC (>8M voters), KS. tl.e: DECLASSIFIED BY COUNSEL TO THE PRESIDENT WARRINGTON ON 10 JULY 2026 on the PRC voter-data reports (18 States, 200M, 6 States, 7 States, Mid-2020 databases, 2019 analysis, 2023 targeting, 2020 public-info), Summaries, PDB, CIA WIRe, Oct 7 emails, FBI ICA comments; "APPROVED FOR PUBLIC RELEASE" on the FBI Albany handout and CIA Venezuela note. Originating agencies masked as "SENSITIVE GOVERNMENT AGENCY." The same day's stamp "APPROVED FOR PUBLIC RELEASE BY COUNSEL TO THE PRESIDENT WARRINGTON on 10 July 2026" is on every page of the 25-document Michigan FBI/PIN file (B14).
Warrington declassifies the 82-page Election Day 2020 watch log (stamp on every page); it is released Aug 6 in the Maricopa packet.
tl.a: Counsel to the President David Warrington

tl.e: Counsel to the President Warrington declassifies the Mar 13, 2020 NSA email chain (every page stamped "DECLASSIFIED BY COUNSEL TO THE PRESIDENT WARRINGTON ON 12 AUGUST 2026").
Board of Peace announced: Trump chair; founding board incl. Rubio, Witkoff, Kushner, Blair, Rowan, Banga, Gabriel.
OCC conditional preliminary charter for World Liberty Trust Company (Zach Witkoff CEO).

Disclosure details: 40 subjects a day, "twelve minutes" each, "all 50 states," "there will be U.S. citizens in this population"; supplied dates had to be used. The disclosure went from counsel (Democracy Defenders Fund) to Sen. Padilla, Rules Committee ranking member, on Sept 8, copied to Sens. McConnell, Grassley and Durbin.
Senators ask DHS IG to examine USCIS searches of California voter site.
Essayli posts on X (Oct 15, 9:08 PM; Oct 16, 5:27 PM and 7:21 PM) about the California matter; Morelle and Padilla cite the posts as showing partisan motivation.
tl.a: C.D. Cal. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli

tl.e: Morelle (House Administration ranking) and Padilla (Senate Rules ranking) write Acting DAG McCotter about the Oct 13 letters, Oct 15 complaint and Oct 16 letter to LA County Counsel, alleging "political weaponization"; they demand answers by 5:00 p.m. Nov 2 on White House direction, how DHS/DOJ built the list, whether private parties supplied data, why DOJ waited, who drafted, private-party input on the legal theory, the "likelihood" threshold and full matching methodology, whether DHS personnel posed as California voters to access voter data, any NVRA 90-day analysis, OPR/ethics consultation, and the thumb-drive cybersecurity and who approved it.
Deadline (5:00 p.m.) for DOJ to answer the Morelle-Padilla Oct 19 questions on the California list and suit.

En bloc confirmation of IGs: Bell (HHS), Moring (DoD), Walk (USDA, ex-senior adviser to USDA Secretary), D'Esposito (Labor, ex-GOP congressman), Kirk (SBA, also PRAC chair from Mar 1, 2026); sworn Dec 22, 2025-Jan 6, 2026.

Inspectors general announce they have joined the NFDC (Aug 25): DOL OIG (IG Anthony P. D'Esposito) says that "As a signatory of the NFDC Charter" it "committed dedicated analysts and investigators to the prosecutor-led effort," describes NFDC as a centralized space joining federal law enforcement, the IG community and state partners, and says the launch turns "the White House Fraud Task Force's whole-of-government approach into a working reality"; SSA OIG says it can "fuse Social Security-specific intelligence with investigative data from across the federal enforcement community"; PRAC is "bringing its data and analytical capabilities to this partnership." The charter text is not public.

Commerce Secretary Lutnick signs (Sept 8, 2026; published Sept 10, 91 FR 57524, FR Doc. 2026-18481; docket USBC-2026-0628, RIN 0607-AA75; OMB-reviewed significant action) the proposed 2030 census residence criteria: usual residence is where a person has "lawfully spent the greatest number of days" in a Jan 3-Apr 1 "census enumeration period," "evidenced by" tax records (sec. 60.2(a)); all foreign citizens other than LPRs are "Not counted for apportionment" (60.4(b)); Census "is considering utilizing its enormously broad access to administrative records to determine an individual's legal status," calling its holdings "nearly exhaustive of the civilian Federal government's holdings" (Treasury, HHS, DHS, State, War, USPS, state and commercial data), and asks comment on a legal-status question; Part 70 bans race, ethnicity and sexual-orientation questions and 70.3(b) bars noise infusion affecting national/state counts (with DAO 216-26). It cites EO 14151, 14192, 14281, the Jul 21, 2020 apportionment memorandum and OMB M-25-20. Comments were due Oct 13, extended to Nov 2 (FR 2026-20328, Oct 5).
